S(\cdot)\in\mathbb{R}^{l^{\prime}\times n_{q}}
, respectively.
Next, we define the following scalar Itô process:

\displaystyle\hat{S}_{i}(t)=\int_{0}^{t}S_{i}(\varsigma)dQ_{\varsigma},\quad d\hat{S}_{i}(t)=S_{i}(t)dQ_{t},\quad t\in[0,T],\quad\hat{S}_{i}(0)=0,\quad i\in\left\{1,\dots,l^{\prime}\right\},

(B.5)

using which we derive the following expression:

\int_{0}^{t}\left(\hat{L}_{j,i}(t)-\hat{L}_{j,i}(\nu)\right)S_{i}(\nu)dQ_{\nu}=\int_{0}^{t}\left(\hat{L}_{j,i}(t)-\hat{L}_{j,i}(\nu)\right)d\hat{S}_{i}(\nu)\\
\begin{multlined}=\hat{L}_{j,i}(t)\int_{0}^{t}d\hat{S}_{i}(\nu)-\int_{0}^{t}\hat{L}_{j,i}(\nu)d\hat{S}_{i}(\nu)\\
=\hat{L}_{j,i}(t)\hat{S}_{i}(t)-\int_{0}^{t}\hat{L}_{j,i}(\nu)d\hat{S}_{i}(\nu),\end{multlined}=\hat{L}_{j,i}(t)\int_{0}^{t}d\hat{S}_{i}(\nu)-\int_{0}^{t}\hat{L}_{j,i}(\nu)d\hat{S}_{i}(\nu)\\
=\hat{L}_{j,i}(t)\hat{S}_{i}(t)-\int_{0}^{t}\hat{L}_{j,i}(\nu)d\hat{S}_{i}(\nu),

(B.6)

for
(j,i,t)\in\left\{1,\dots,l\right\}\times\left\{1,\dots,l^{\prime}\right\}\times[0,T]
.
It is clear that
\hat{L}_{j,i}(t)
is
\mathfrak{F}_{t}
-adapted due its definition in (
B.2
) and the assumed adaptedness of
L
.
Moreover, we may write
\hat{L}_{j,i}(t)=\hat{L}_{j,i}^{+}(t)-\hat{L}_{j,i}^{-}(t)
, where

\displaystyle\hat{L}_{j,i}^{+}(t)=\int_{0}^{t}\max\left\{0,L_{j,i}(\varsigma)\right\}d\varsigma,\quad\hat{L}_{j,i}^{-}(t)=\int_{0}^{t}\max\left\{-L_{j,i}(\varsigma),0\right\}d\varsigma.

Since both
\hat{L}_{j,i}^{+}(t)
and
\hat{L}_{j,i}^{-}(t)
are increasing processes, we conclude that
\hat{L}_{j,i}(t)
is a finite variation process
[
91
, Sec. 1.3]
.
Therefore we may use the integration by parts formula
[
91
, Thm. 1.6.5]
to obtain

\displaystyle\int_{0}^{t}\hat{L}_{j,i}(\nu)d\hat{S}_{i}(\nu)=\hat{L}_{j,i}(t)\hat{S}_{i}(t)-\int_{0}^{t}\hat{S}_{i}(\nu)d\hat{L}_{j,i}(\nu),

where the last integral is a Lebesgue-Stieltjes integral.
Substituting the above equality into (
B.6
), we obtain

\displaystyle\int_{0}^{t}\left(\hat{L}_{j,i}(t)-\hat{L}_{j,i}(\nu)\right)S_{i}(\nu)dQ_{\nu}=\hat{L}_{j,i}(t)\hat{S}_{i}(t)-\int_{0}^{t}\hat{L}_{j,i}(\nu)d\hat{S}_{i}(\nu)=\int_{0}^{t}\hat{S}_{i}(\nu)d\hat{L}_{j,i}(\nu),

(B.7)

for
(j,i,t)\in\left\{1,\dots,l\right\}\times\left\{1,\dots,l^{\prime}\right\}\times[0,T]
.
Then, once again appealing to the decomposition
\hat{L}_{j,i}(t)=\hat{L}_{j,i}^{+}(t)-\hat{L}_{j,i}^{-}(t)
, and using the continuity of
L
and the definition of
\hat{L}
in (
B.2
), we apply the fundamental theorem for Lebesgue-Stieltjes integrals
[
113
, Thm. 7.7.1]
to (
B.7
) and obtain

\displaystyle\int_{0}^{t}\left(\hat{L}_{j,i}(t)-\hat{L}_{j,i}(\nu)\right)S_{i}(\nu)dQ_{\nu}=\int_{0}^{t}\hat{S}_{i}(\nu)d\hat{L}_{j,i}(\nu)=\int_{0}^{t}\hat{S}_{i}(\nu)L_{j,i}(\nu)d\nu,

for
(j,i,t)\in\left\{1,\dots,l\right\}\times\left\{1,\dots,l^{\prime}\right\}\times[0,T]
.
The proof of (
B.1a
) is then concluded by substituting the above expression into (
B.4
)
to obtain

\begin{aligned} &\int_{0}^{t}\int_{\nu}^{t}L(\beta)S(\nu)d\beta dQ_{\nu}\\
&=\sum_{i=1}^{l^{\prime}}\int_{0}^{t}\begin{bmatrix}\left(\hat{L}_{1,i}(t)-\hat{L}_{1,i}(\nu)\right)S_{i}(\nu)dQ_{\nu}&\cdots&\left(\hat{L}_{l,i}(t)-\hat{L}_{l,i}(\nu)\right)S_{i}(\nu)dQ_{\nu}\end{bmatrix}^{\top}\\
&=\sum_{i=1}^{l^{\prime}}\int_{0}^{t}\begin{bmatrix}\hat{S}_{i}(\nu)L_{1,i}(\nu)d\nu&\cdots&\hat{S}_{i}(\nu)L_{l,i}(\nu)d\nu\end{bmatrix}^{\top}\end{aligned}\\
\overset{(\star)}{=}\sum_{i=1}^{l^{\prime}}\int_{0}^{t}\int_{0}^{\nu}\begin{bmatrix}L_{1,i}(\nu)S_{i}(\beta)dQ_{\beta}d\nu&\cdots&L_{l,i}(\nu)S_{i}(\beta)dQ_{\beta}d\nu\end{bmatrix}^{\top}=\int_{0}^{t}\int_{0}^{\nu}L(\nu)S(\beta)dQ_{\beta}d\nu,

where the equality
(\star)
is obtained by invoking the definition of the scalar process
\hat{S}_{i}(t)
in (
B.5
).
∎

The next result is a straightforward moment bound for the Lebesgue integral of pertinent stochastic processes.

Proposition B.1

Consider a complete filtered probability space
\left(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P}\right)
with filtration
\mathfrak{F}_{t}
, and let
S\in\mathcal{M}_{2}^{loc}\left(\mathbb{R}^{n_{s}}|\mathfrak{F}_{t}\right)
satisfy

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\int_{0}^{T}\left\|S(\nu)\right\|^{{\mathsf{p}}}d\nu\right]<\infty,\quad\forall{\mathsf{p}}\geq 1.

Additionally, for any constants
\theta\in\mathbb{R}_{>0}
and
\xi\in[0,T]
, define

N(t)=\int_{\xi}^{t}e^{\theta\nu}\left\|S(\nu)\right\|d\nu\in\mathbb{R},\quad t\in[\xi,T].

Then,

\left\|N(t)\right\|_{L_{{\mathsf{p}}}}\leq\frac{e^{\theta t}-e^{\theta\xi}}{\theta}\sup_{\nu\in[\xi,t]}\left\|S(\nu)\right\|_{L_{{\mathsf{p}}}},\quad\forall(t,{\mathsf{p}})\in[\xi,T]\times\mathbb{N}_{\geq 1}.

(B.8)

Proof.

For
{\mathsf{p}}=1
, we use the Fubini’s theorem to conclude that

\mathbb{E}\left[N(t)\right]=\int_{\xi}^{t}e^{\theta\nu}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|S(\nu)\right\|\right]d\nu\leq\left(\int_{\xi}^{t}e^{\theta\nu}d\nu\right)\sup_{\nu\in[\xi,t]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|S(\nu)\right\|\right]=\frac{e^{\theta t}-e^{\theta\xi}}{\theta}\sup_{\nu\in[\xi,t]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|S(\nu)\right\|\right],

for all
t\in[\xi,T]
, thus establishing (
B.8
).
For
{\mathsf{p}}\in\mathbb{N}_{\geq 2}
, we obtain the following chain of inequalities:

\displaystyle\left\|N(t)\right\|_{L_{{\mathsf{p}}}}=\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\int_{\xi}^{t}e^{\theta\nu}\left\|S(\nu)\right\|d\nu\right)^{\mathsf{p}}\right]^{\frac{1}{{\mathsf{p}}}}\overset{(\star)}{\leq}\int_{\xi}^{t}e^{\theta\nu}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|S(\nu)\right\|^{\mathsf{p}}\right]^{\frac{1}{{\mathsf{p}}}}d\nu\leq\left(\int_{\xi}^{t}e^{\theta\nu}d\nu\right)\sup_{\nu\in[\xi,t]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|S(\nu)\right\|^{\mathsf{p}}\right]^{\frac{1}{{\mathsf{p}}}},

for all
t\in[\xi,T]
, where
(\star)
follows from the Minkowski’s integral inequality
[
114
, Thm. 202]
.
The bound in (
B.8
),
\forall{\mathsf{p}}\in\mathbb{N}_{\geq 2}
, then follows by solving the integral.

∎

The following is a simple corollary of the last result.

Corollary B.1

Let the hypotheses of Proposition
B.1
hold.
Then, the process

N(t)=\int_{\xi}^{t}\left\|S(\nu)\right\|d\nu\in\mathbb{R},\quad t\in[\xi,T],

satisfies

\left\|N(t)\right\|_{L_{{\mathsf{p}}}}\leq(t-\xi)\sup_{\nu\in[\xi,t]}\left\|S(\nu)\right\|_{L_{{\mathsf{p}}}},\quad\forall(t,{\mathsf{p}})\in[\xi,T]\times\mathbb{N}_{\geq 1}.

(B.9)

Proof.

The proof follows by noting that
N(t)
in this corollary can be obtained from
N(t)
in Proposition
B.1
by setting
\theta=0
.

∎

Next, we apply Proposition
B.1
to obtain a moment bound for nested Lebesgue integrals.

Proposition B.2

Consider a complete filtered probability space
\left(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P}\right)
with filtration
\mathfrak{F}_{t}
, and let
S_{1}\in\mathcal{M}_{2}^{loc}\left(\mathbb{R}^{n_{1}}|\mathfrak{F}_{t}\right)
and
S_{2}\in\mathcal{M}_{2}^{loc}\left(\mathbb{R}^{n_{2}}|\mathfrak{F}_{t}\right)
satisfy

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\int_{0}^{T}\left[\left\|S_{1}(\nu)\right\|^{2{\mathsf{p}}}+\left\|S_{2}(\nu)\right\|^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]d\nu\right]<\infty,\quad\forall{\mathsf{p}}\geq 1.

Additionally, for any constants
\theta_{1}\in\mathbb{R}_{>0}
,
\theta_{2}\in\mathbb{R}_{>0}
, and
\xi\in[0,T]
, define

N(t)=\int_{\xi}^{t}e^{(\theta_{1}-\theta_{2})\nu}\left\|S_{1}(\nu)\right\|\left(\int_{0}^{\nu}e^{\theta_{2}\beta}\left\|S_{2}(\beta)\right\|d\beta\right)d\nu\in\mathbb{R},\quad t\in[\xi,T].

Then,

\left\|N(t)\right\|_{L_{{\mathsf{p}}}}\leq\frac{e^{\theta_{1}t}-e^{\theta_{1}\xi}}{\theta_{1}\theta_{2}}\sup_{\nu\in[\xi,t]}\left\|S_{1}(\nu)\right\|_{L_{2{\mathsf{p}}}}\sup_{\nu\in[0,t]}\left\|S_{2}(\nu)\right\|_{L_{2{\mathsf{p}}}},\quad\forall(t,{\mathsf{p}})\in[\xi,T]\times\mathbb{N}_{\geq 1}.

(B.10)

Proof.

We begin with the case
{\mathsf{p}}=1
, for which we apply Fubini’s theorem, followed by the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality to obtain

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left|N(t)\right|\right]=

\displaystyle\int_{\xi}^{t}e^{(\theta_{1}-\theta_{2})\nu}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|S_{1}(\nu)\right\|\left(\int_{0}^{\nu}e^{\theta_{2}\beta}\left\|S_{2}(\beta)\right\|d\beta\right)\right]d\nu

\displaystyle\leq

\displaystyle\int_{\xi}^{t}e^{(\theta_{1}-\theta_{2})\nu}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|S_{1}(\nu)\right\|^{2}\right]^{\frac{1}{2}}\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\int_{0}^{\nu}e^{\theta_{2}\beta}\left\|S_{2}(\beta)\right\|d\beta\right)^{2}\right]^{\frac{1}{2}}d\nu,\quad\forall t\in[\xi,T],

where we have used the fact that, by definition,
N(t)\geq 0
,
\forall t\geq\xi
.
Applying Proposition
B.1
to the second inner integral with
\left\{\theta,\xi,n_{s},S\right\}=\left\{\theta_{2},0,n_{2},S_{2}\right\}
leads to

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left|N(t)\right|\right]\leq

\displaystyle\frac{1}{\theta_{2}}\int_{\xi}^{t}\left(e^{\theta_{1}\nu}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|S_{1}(\nu)\right\|^{2}\right]^{\frac{1}{2}}\sup_{\beta\in[0,\nu]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|S_{2}(\beta)\right\|^{2}\right]^{\frac{1}{2}}\right)d\nu

\displaystyle\leq

\displaystyle\frac{1}{\theta_{2}}\left(\int_{\xi}^{t}e^{\theta_{1}\nu}d\nu\right)\sup_{\nu\in[\xi,t]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|S_{1}(\nu)\right\|^{2}\right]^{\frac{1}{2}}\sup_{\nu\in[0,t]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|S_{2}(\nu)\right\|^{2}\right]^{\frac{1}{2}},\quad\forall t\in[\xi,T],

where in the first inequality we have used the bound
1-e^{-\theta_{2}\nu}\leq 1
,
\nu\in[\xi,t]
.
Solving the integral on the right hand side then leads to (
B.10
) for
{\mathsf{p}}=1
.

Next, we consider the
L_{\mathsf{p}}
norm of
N(t)
for
{\mathsf{p}}\in\mathbb{N}_{\geq 2}
given by

\displaystyle\left\|N(t)\right\|_{L_{{\mathsf{p}}}}=\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\int_{\xi}^{t}e^{(\theta_{1}-\theta_{2})\nu}\left\|S_{1}(\nu)\right\|\left(\int_{0}^{\nu}e^{\theta_{2}\beta}\left\|S_{2}(\beta)\right\|d\beta\right)d\nu\right)^{\mathsf{p}}\right]^{\frac{1}{{\mathsf{p}}}},\quad\forall t\in[\xi,T].

From Minkowski’s integral inequality
[
114
, Thm. 202]
, we get

\displaystyle\left\|N(t)\right\|_{L_{{\mathsf{p}}}}=

\displaystyle\,\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\int_{\xi}^{t}e^{(\theta_{1}-\theta_{2})\nu}\left\|S_{1}(\nu)\right\|\left(\int_{0}^{\nu}e^{\theta_{2}\beta}\left\|S_{2}(\beta)\right\|d\beta\right)d\nu\right)^{\mathsf{p}}\right]^{\frac{1}{{\mathsf{p}}}}

\displaystyle\leq

\displaystyle\int_{\xi}^{t}e^{\left(\theta_{1}-\theta_{2}\right)\nu}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|S_{1}(\nu)\right\|^{\mathsf{p}}\left(\int_{0}^{\nu}e^{\theta_{2}\beta}\left\|S_{2}(\beta)\right\|d\beta\right)^{\mathsf{p}}\right]^{\frac{1}{{\mathsf{p}}}}d\nu,

for all
t\in[\xi,T]
.
Subsequently, applying the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality then leads to

\displaystyle\left\|N(t)\right\|_{L_{{\mathsf{p}}}}\leq\int_{\xi}^{t}e^{\left(\theta_{1}-\theta_{2}\right)\nu}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|S_{1}(\nu)\right\|^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{2{\mathsf{p}}}}\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\int_{0}^{\nu}e^{\theta_{2}\beta}\left\|S_{2}(\beta)\right\|d\beta\right)^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{2{\mathsf{p}}}}d\nu,\quad\forall t\in[\xi,T].

(B.11)

Next, using Proposition
B.1
for
\left\{\theta,\xi,n_{s},S\right\}=\left\{\theta_{2},0,n_{2},S_{2}\right\}
, we obtain

\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\int_{0}^{\nu}e^{\theta_{2}\beta}\left\|S_{2}(\beta)\right\|d\beta\right)^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{2{\mathsf{p}}}}\leq\left(\frac{e^{\theta_{2}\nu}-1}{\theta_{2}}\right)\sup_{\beta\in[0,\nu]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|S_{2}(\beta)\right\|^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{2{\mathsf{p}}}}\\
\leq\frac{e^{\theta_{2}\nu}}{\theta_{2}}\sup_{\beta\in[0,\nu]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|S_{2}(\beta)\right\|^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{2{\mathsf{p}}}},\quad\forall\nu\in[\xi,t],

where we have bounded
e^{\theta_{2}\nu}-1
by
e^{\theta_{2}\nu}
.
Substituting the above bound in (
B.11
) yields

\displaystyle\left\|N(t)\right\|_{L_{{\mathsf{p}}}}\leq

\displaystyle\frac{1}{\theta_{2}}\int_{\xi}^{t}e^{\theta_{1}\nu}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|S_{1}(\nu)\right\|^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{2{\mathsf{p}}}}\sup_{\beta\in[0,\nu]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|S_{2}(\beta)\right\|^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{2{\mathsf{p}}}}d\nu

\displaystyle\leq

\displaystyle\frac{1}{\theta_{2}}\left(\int_{\xi}^{t}e^{\theta_{1}\nu}d\nu\right)^{\frac{1}{{\mathsf{p}}}}\sup_{\nu\in[\xi,t]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|S_{1}(\nu)\right\|^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{2{\mathsf{p}}}}\sup_{\nu\in[0,t]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|S_{2}(\nu)\right\|^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{2{\mathsf{p}}}},

\displaystyle\leq

\displaystyle\frac{e^{\theta_{1}t}-e^{\theta_{1}\xi}}{\theta_{1}\theta_{2}}\sup_{\nu\in[\xi,t]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|S_{1}(\nu)\right\|^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{2{\mathsf{p}}}}\sup_{\nu\in[0,t]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|S_{2}(\nu)\right\|^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{2{\mathsf{p}}}},\quad\forall t\in[\xi,T],

which establishes (
B.10
) for all
{\mathsf{p}}\in\mathbb{N}_{\geq 2}
.

∎

The following result provides moment bound for a pertinent class of Itô integrals.

Lemma B.2

Consider a complete filtered probability space
\left(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P}\right)
with filtration
\mathfrak{F}_{t}
, and let
L\in\mathcal{M}_{2}^{loc}\left(\mathbb{R}^{n_{l}\times n_{q}}|\mathfrak{F}_{t}\right)
satisfy

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\int_{0}^{T}\left\|L(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{{\mathsf{p}}}d\nu\right]<\infty,\quad\forall{\mathsf{p}}\geq 2.

Additionally, for any constants
\theta\in\mathbb{R}_{>0}
and
\xi\in[0,T]
, and an
\mathfrak{F}_{t}
-adapted Brownian motion
Q_{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{n_{q}}
, define

N(t)=\int_{\xi}^{t}e^{\theta\nu}L(\nu)dQ_{\nu}\in\mathbb{R}^{n_{l}},\quad t\in[\xi,T].

Then,

\displaystyle\left\|N(t)\right\|_{L_{{\mathsf{p}}}}\leq

\displaystyle\left({\mathsf{p}}\frac{{\mathsf{p}}-1}{2}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\left(\frac{e^{2\theta t}-e^{2\theta\xi}}{2\theta}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\sup_{\nu\in[\xi,t]}\left\|L(\nu)\right\|_{L_{{\mathsf{p}}}},\quad\forall(t,{\mathsf{p}})\in[\xi,T]\times\mathbb{N}_{\geq 2}.

(B.12)

Proof.

We begin with the case when
{\mathsf{p}}=2
.
Since
\xi\in[0,T]
is a constant, and hence a stopping time, we use Itô isometry
[
91
, Thm. 1.5.21]
to obtain

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|N(t)\right\|^{2}\right]=\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|\int_{\xi}^{t}e^{\theta\nu}L(\nu)dQ_{\nu}\right\|^{2}\right]=\mathbb{E}\left[\int_{\xi}^{t}e^{2\theta\nu}\left\|L(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{2}d\nu\right].

It then follows from Fubini’s theorem that

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|N(t)\right\|^{2}\right]\leq\int_{\xi}^{t}e^{2\theta\nu}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|L(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{2}\right]d\nu\leq

\displaystyle\left(\int_{\xi}^{t}e^{2\theta\nu}d\nu\right)\sup_{\nu\in[\xi,t]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|L(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{2}\right]

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\frac{e^{2\theta t}-e^{2\theta\xi}}{2\theta}\sup_{\nu\in[\xi,t]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|L(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{2}\right],\quad\forall t\in[\xi,T],

which establishes (
B.12
) for
{\mathsf{p}}=2
.

Next, let
{\mathsf{p}}\in\mathbb{N}_{>2}
.
Using Itô’s lemma
[
91
, Thm. 1.6.4]
in a similar fashion to the proof of
[
91
, Thm. 1.7.1]
, we get

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|N(t)\right\|^{{\mathsf{p}}}\right]=\frac{{\mathsf{p}}}{2}\mathbb{E}\left[\int_{\xi}^{t}\left(\left\|N(\nu)\right\|^{{\mathsf{p}}-2}e^{2\theta\nu}\left\|L(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{2}+({\mathsf{p}}-2)\left\|N(\nu)\right\|^{{\mathsf{p}}-4}e^{2\theta\nu}\left\|N(\nu)^{\top}L(\nu)\right\|^{2}\right)d\nu\right],

(B.13)

for
t\in[\xi,T]
.
Thus, we obtain the following bound using the submultiplicativity of norms:

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|N(t)\right\|^{{\mathsf{p}}}\right]\leq

\displaystyle{\mathsf{p}}\frac{{\mathsf{p}}-1}{2}\mathbb{E}\left[\int_{\xi}^{t}\left\|N(\nu)\right\|^{{\mathsf{p}}-2}e^{2\theta\nu}\left\|L(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{2}d\nu\right]

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle{\mathsf{p}}\frac{{\mathsf{p}}-1}{2}\mathbb{E}\left[\int_{\xi}^{t}e^{2\theta\nu({\mathsf{p}}-2)/{\mathsf{p}}}\left\|N(\nu)\right\|^{{\mathsf{p}}-2}e^{4\theta\nu/{\mathsf{p}}}\left\|L(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{2}d\nu\right],\quad\forall t\in[\xi,T],

where we obtain the last expression by writing
e^{2\theta\nu}=e^{2\theta\nu\left[({\mathsf{p}}-2)/{\mathsf{p}}+2/{\mathsf{p}}\right]}=e^{2\theta\nu({\mathsf{p}}-2)/{\mathsf{p}}}e^{4\theta\nu/{\mathsf{p}}}
.
Using Hölder’s inequality with conjugates
{\mathsf{p}}/({\mathsf{p}}-2)
and
{\mathsf{p}}/2
, followed by Fubini’s theorem, leads to

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|N(t)\right\|^{{\mathsf{p}}}\right]\leq

\displaystyle{\mathsf{p}}\frac{{\mathsf{p}}-1}{2}\mathbb{E}\left[\int_{\xi}^{t}e^{2\theta\nu}\left\|N(\nu)\right\|^{{\mathsf{p}}}d\nu\right]^{\frac{{\mathsf{p}}-2}{{\mathsf{p}}}}\mathbb{E}\left[\int_{\xi}^{t}e^{2\theta\nu}\left\|L(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{{\mathsf{p}}}d\nu\right]^{\frac{2}{{\mathsf{p}}}}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle{\mathsf{p}}\frac{{\mathsf{p}}-1}{2}\left(\int_{\xi}^{t}e^{2\theta\nu}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|N(\nu)\right\|^{{\mathsf{p}}}\right]d\nu\right)^{\frac{{\mathsf{p}}-2}{{\mathsf{p}}}}\left(\int_{\xi}^{t}e^{2\theta\nu}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|L(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{{\mathsf{p}}}\right]d\nu\right)^{\frac{2}{{\mathsf{p}}}},\quad\forall t\in[\xi,T].

Note from (
B.13
) that
\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|N(t)\right\|^{{\mathsf{p}}}\right]
is non-decreasing in
t
.
It then follows that

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|N(t)\right\|^{{\mathsf{p}}}\right]\leq

\displaystyle{\mathsf{p}}\frac{{\mathsf{p}}-1}{2}\left(\int_{\xi}^{t}e^{2\theta\nu}d\nu\right)^{\frac{{\mathsf{p}}-2}{{\mathsf{p}}}}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|N(t)\right\|^{{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{{\mathsf{p}}-2}{{\mathsf{p}}}}\left(\int_{\xi}^{t}e^{2\theta\nu}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|L(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{{\mathsf{p}}}\right]d\nu\right)^{\frac{2}{{\mathsf{p}}}}

\displaystyle\leq

\displaystyle{\mathsf{p}}\frac{{\mathsf{p}}-1}{2}\left(\int_{\xi}^{t}e^{2\theta\nu}d\nu\right)^{\frac{{\mathsf{p}}-2}{{\mathsf{p}}}}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|N(t)\right\|^{{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{{\mathsf{p}}-2}{{\mathsf{p}}}}\left(\int_{\xi}^{t}e^{2\theta\nu}d\nu\right)^{\frac{2}{{\mathsf{p}}}}\sup_{\nu\in[\xi,t]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|L(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{2}{{\mathsf{p}}}}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle{\mathsf{p}}\frac{{\mathsf{p}}-1}{2}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|N(t)\right\|^{{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{{\mathsf{p}}-2}{{\mathsf{p}}}}\left(\int_{\xi}^{t}e^{2\theta\nu}d\nu\right)\sup_{\nu\in[\xi,t]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|L(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{2}{{\mathsf{p}}}},\quad\forall t\in[\xi,T],

and thus

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|N(t)\right\|^{{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{2}{{\mathsf{p}}}}\leq

\displaystyle{\mathsf{p}}\frac{{\mathsf{p}}-1}{2}\left(\int_{\xi}^{t}e^{2\theta\nu}d\nu\right)\sup_{\nu\in[\xi,t]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|L(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{2}{{\mathsf{p}}}}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle{\mathsf{p}}\frac{{\mathsf{p}}-1}{2}\frac{e^{2\theta t}-e^{2\theta\xi}}{2\theta}\sup_{\nu\in[\xi,t]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|L(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{2}{{\mathsf{p}}}},\quad\forall t\in[\xi,T],

which proves (
B.12
),
\forall{\mathsf{p}}\in\mathbb{N}_{>2}
.

∎

Next, we provide a bound on a particular Lebesgue integral with an Itô integral in the integrand.

Lemma B.3

Consider a complete filtered probability space
\left(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P}\right)
with filtration
\mathfrak{F}_{t}
, and let
S\in\mathcal{M}_{2}^{loc}\left(\mathbb{R}^{n_{s}}|\mathfrak{F}_{t}\right)
and
L\in\mathcal{M}_{2}^{loc}\left(\mathbb{R}^{n_{l}\times n_{q}}|\mathfrak{F}_{t}\right)
satisfy

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\int_{0}^{T}\left(\left\|S(\nu)\right\|^{2{\mathsf{p}}}+\left\|L(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right)d\nu\right]<\infty,\quad\forall{\mathsf{p}}\geq 1.

Additionally, for any
\theta_{1},\,\theta_{2}\in\mathbb{R}_{>0}
,
\xi\in\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}
, and an
\mathfrak{F}_{t}
-adapted Brownian motion
Q_{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{n_{q}}
define

N(t)=\int_{\xi}^{t}e^{(\theta_{1}-\theta_{2})\nu}\left\|S(\nu)\right\|\left\|\int_{0}^{\nu}e^{\theta_{2}\beta}\mathbbm{1}_{[\zeta_{1},\zeta_{2}]}\left(\beta\right)L(\beta)dQ_{\beta}\right\|d\nu\in\mathbb{R},\quad t\in[\xi,T],

where and
0\leq\zeta_{1}\leq\zeta_{2}\leq t
are any deterministic variables.
Then,

\displaystyle\left\|N(t)\right\|_{L_{{\mathsf{p}}}}\leq\left({\mathsf{p}}\frac{2{\mathsf{p}}-1}{2}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\frac{e^{\theta_{1}t}-e^{\theta_{1}(\xi\vee\zeta_{1})}}{\theta_{1}\sqrt{\theta_{2}}}\left(1-e^{-2\theta_{2}(\zeta_{2}-\zeta_{1})}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\sup_{\nu\in[\xi,t]}\left\|S(\nu)\right\|_{L_{2{\mathsf{p}}}}\sup_{\nu\in[\zeta_{1},\zeta_{2}]}\left\|L(\nu)\right\|_{L_{2{\mathsf{p}}}},

(B.14)

for all
(t,{\mathsf{p}})\in[\xi,T]\times\mathbb{N}_{\geq 1}
.

Proof.

We provide the proof only for the case when
{\mathsf{p}}\in\mathbb{N}_{\geq 2}
, since the proof for
{\mathsf{p}}=1
is established
mutatis mutandis
.
The presence of the indicator function in the inner integrand allows us to write

N(t)=\int_{\xi}^{t}e^{(\theta_{1}-\theta_{2})\nu}\left\|S(\nu)\right\|\left\|\int_{0}^{\nu}e^{\theta_{2}\beta}\mathbbm{1}_{[\zeta_{1},\zeta_{2}]}\left(\beta\right)L(\beta)dQ_{\beta}\right\|d\nu\\
=\int_{\xi\vee\zeta_{1}}^{t}e^{(\theta_{1}-\theta_{2})\nu}\left\|S(\nu)\right\|\left\|\int_{\zeta_{1}}^{\nu\wedge\zeta_{2}}e^{\theta_{2}\beta}L(\beta)dQ_{\beta}\right\|d\nu,\quad t\in[\xi,T].

Now, consider the
L_{\mathsf{p}}
norm of
N(t)
.
By following the same line of reasoning that led to (
B.11
) in the proof of Proposition
B.2
, we obtain:

\displaystyle\left\|N(t)\right\|_{L_{{\mathsf{p}}}}\leq\int_{\xi\vee\zeta_{1}}^{t}e^{\left(\theta_{1}-\theta_{2}\right)\nu}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|S(\nu)\right\|^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{2{\mathsf{p}}}}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|\int_{\zeta_{1}}^{\nu\wedge\zeta_{2}}e^{\theta_{2}\beta}L(\beta)dQ_{\beta}\right\|^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{2{\mathsf{p}}}}d\nu,\quad t\in[\xi,T].

Next, using Lemma
B.2
for
\left\{\theta,\xi,t\right\}=\left\{\theta_{2},\zeta_{1},\nu\wedge\zeta_{2}\right\}
leads to

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|\int_{\zeta_{1}}^{\nu\wedge\zeta_{2}}e^{\theta_{2}\beta}L(\beta)dQ_{\beta}\right\|^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{2{\mathsf{p}}}}\leq

\displaystyle\left({\mathsf{p}}\frac{2{\mathsf{p}}-1}{2\theta_{2}}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\left(e^{2\theta_{2}(\nu\wedge\zeta_{2})}-e^{2\theta_{2}\zeta_{1}}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\sup_{\beta\in[\zeta_{1},\nu\wedge\zeta_{2}]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|L(\beta)\right\|^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{2{\mathsf{p}}}}

\displaystyle\leq

\displaystyle\left({\mathsf{p}}\frac{2{\mathsf{p}}-1}{2\theta_{2}}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\left(e^{2\theta_{2}(\nu\wedge\zeta_{2})}-e^{2\theta_{2}\zeta_{1}}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\sup_{\beta\in[\zeta_{1},\zeta_{2}]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|L(\beta)\right\|^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{2{\mathsf{p}}}},

for all
\nu\in[\xi,t]
, where the last inequality follows from the fact that
[\zeta_{1},\nu\wedge\zeta_{2}]\subseteq[\zeta_{1},\zeta_{2}]
,
\forall\nu\in[\xi,t]
.
Therefore,

\left\|N(t)\right\|_{L_{{\mathsf{p}}}}\leq\int_{\xi\vee\zeta_{1}}^{t}e^{\left(\theta_{1}-\theta_{2}\right)\nu}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|S(\nu)\right\|^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{2{\mathsf{p}}}}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|\int_{\zeta_{1}}^{\nu\wedge\zeta_{2}}e^{\theta_{2}\beta}L(\beta)dQ_{\beta}\right\|^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{2{\mathsf{p}}}}d\nu\\
\leq\left({\mathsf{p}}\frac{2{\mathsf{p}}-1}{2\theta_{2}}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\left(\int_{\xi\vee\zeta_{1}}^{t}e^{\left(\theta_{1}-\theta_{2}\right)\nu}\left(e^{2\theta_{2}(\nu\wedge\zeta_{2})}-e^{2\theta_{2}\zeta_{1}}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}d\nu\right)\\
\times\sup_{\nu\in[\xi,t]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|S(\nu)\right\|^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{2{\mathsf{p}}}}\sup_{\nu\in[\zeta_{1},\zeta_{2}]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|L(\nu)\right\|^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{2{\mathsf{p}}}},

(B.15)

for all
t\in[\xi,T]
, where we have used the fact that
[\xi\vee\zeta_{1},t]\subseteq[\xi,t]
.
The definition
(\nu\wedge\zeta_{2})\doteq\min(\nu,\zeta_{2})
implies that
(\nu\wedge\zeta_{2})\leq\nu
and
(\nu\wedge\zeta_{2})\leq\zeta_{2}
.
Hence,

\displaystyle\left(e^{2\theta_{2}(\nu\wedge\zeta_{2})}-e^{2\theta_{2}\zeta_{1}}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}=e^{\theta_{2}(\nu\wedge\zeta_{2})}\left(1-e^{-2\theta_{2}((\nu\wedge\zeta_{2})-\zeta_{1})}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\leq e^{\theta_{2}\nu}\left(1-e^{-2\theta_{2}(\zeta_{2}-\zeta_{1})}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}.

This bound allows us to further develop the following:

\displaystyle\int_{\xi\vee\zeta_{1}}^{t}e^{\left(\theta_{1}-\theta_{2}\right)\nu}\left(e^{2\theta_{2}(\nu\wedge\zeta_{2})}-e^{2\theta_{2}\zeta_{1}}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}d\nu\leq\left(\int_{\xi\vee\zeta_{1}}^{t}e^{\theta_{1}\nu}d\nu\right)\left(1-e^{-2\theta_{2}(\zeta_{2}-\zeta_{1})}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}.

Substituting the above bound in (
B.15
) yields

\left\|N(t)\right\|_{L_{{\mathsf{p}}}}\leq\left({\mathsf{p}}\frac{2{\mathsf{p}}-1}{2\theta_{2}}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\left(\int_{\xi\vee\zeta_{1}}^{t}e^{\theta_{1}\nu}d\nu\right)\left(1-e^{-2\theta_{2}(\zeta_{2}-\zeta_{1})}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\
\times\sup_{\nu\in[\xi,t]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|S(\nu)\right\|^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{2{\mathsf{p}}}}\sup_{\nu\in[\zeta_{1},\zeta_{2}]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|L(\nu)\right\|^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{2{\mathsf{p}}}},

(B.16)

for all
t\in[\xi,T]
.
Solving the integral on the right hand side establishes (
B.14
) for
{\mathsf{p}}\in\mathbb{N}_{\geq 2}
, thus completing the proof.

∎

The following is a corollary of the last result.

Corollary B.2

Consider a complete filtered probability space
\left(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P}\right)
with filtration
\mathfrak{F}_{t}
, and let
S\in\mathcal{M}_{2}^{loc}\left(\mathbb{R}^{n_{s}}|\mathfrak{F}_{t}\right)
and
L\in\mathcal{M}_{2}^{loc}\left(\mathbb{R}^{n_{l}\times n_{q}}|\mathfrak{F}_{t}\right)
satisfy

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\int_{0}^{T}\left(\left\|S(\nu)\right\|^{2{\mathsf{p}}}+\left\|L(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{4{\mathsf{p}}}\right)d\nu\right]<\infty,\quad\forall{\mathsf{p}}\geq 1.

Additionally, for any
\theta_{1},\,\theta_{2}\in\mathbb{R}_{>0}
,
\xi\in\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}
,
{\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}}\in\mathbb{R}_{>0}
, and an
\mathfrak{F}_{t}
-adapted Brownian motion
Q_{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{n_{q}}
define

\displaystyle N_{\left\{a,b\right\}}(t)=\int_{{\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}}}^{t}e^{(\theta_{1}-\theta_{2})\nu}\left\|S(\nu)\right\|\left\|R_{\left\{a,b\right\}}(\nu)\right\|d\nu\in\mathbb{R},\quad t\in[{\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}},T],

where

\displaystyle R_{a}(\nu)=L(\nu)\varsigma_{1}(\nu)\int_{(i^{\star}\left(\nu\right)-1){\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}}}^{i^{\star}\left(\nu\right){\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}}}e^{\theta_{2}\beta}\varsigma_{2}(\beta)dQ_{\beta},\quad R_{b}(\nu)=L(\nu)\int_{i^{\star}\left(\nu\right){\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}}}^{\nu}e^{\theta_{2}\beta}dQ_{\beta},

and where
i^{\star}\left(\nu\right)\doteq\max\left\{i\in\mathbb{N}_{\geq 1}\,:\,i{\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}}\leq\nu\right\}=\left\lfloor\nu/{\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}}\right\rfloor
.
Furthermore,
\varsigma_{\left\{1,2\right\}}\in\mathcal{C}\left(\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0},\mathbb{R}\right)
are any deterministic functions.
Then, for all
(t,{\mathsf{p}})\in[{\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}},T]\times\mathbb{N}_{\geq 1}
:

\left\|N_{a}(t)\right\|_{L_{{\mathsf{p}}}}\leq\left({\mathsf{p}}(4{\mathsf{p}}-1)\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\frac{e^{\theta_{1}t}-e^{\theta_{1}{\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}}}}{\theta_{1}\sqrt{\theta_{2}}}\left(1-e^{-2\theta_{2}{\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}}}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\
\times\sup_{\nu\in[{\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}},t]}\left(\left\|S(\nu)\right\|_{L_{2{\mathsf{p}}}}\left\|L(\nu)\right\|_{L_{4{\mathsf{p}}}}\left|\varsigma_{1}(\nu)\right|\sup_{\beta\in[(i^{\star}\left(\nu\right)-1){\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}},i^{\star}\left(\nu\right){\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}}]}\left|\varsigma_{2}(\beta)\right|\right),

(B.17)

and

\displaystyle\left\|N_{b}(t)\right\|_{L_{{\mathsf{p}}}}\leq\left({\mathsf{p}}(4{\mathsf{p}}-1)\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\frac{e^{\theta_{1}t}-e^{\theta_{1}{\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}}}}{\theta_{1}\sqrt{\theta_{2}}}\left(1-e^{-2\theta_{2}{\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}}}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\sup_{\nu\in[{\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}},t]}\left\|S(\nu)\right\|_{L_{2{\mathsf{p}}}}\sup_{\nu\in[{\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}},t]}\left\|L(\nu)\right\|_{L_{4{\mathsf{p}}}}.

(B.18)

Proof.

We provide the proof only for the case when
{\mathsf{p}}\in\mathbb{N}_{\geq 2}
.
As in the proof of Lemma
B.3
, we have

\displaystyle\left\|N_{\left\{a,b\right\}}(t)\right\|_{L_{{\mathsf{p}}}}\leq\int_{{\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}}}^{t}e^{\left(\theta_{1}-\theta_{2}\right)\nu}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|S(\nu)\right\|^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{2{\mathsf{p}}}}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|R_{\left\{a,b\right\}}(\nu)\right\|^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{2{\mathsf{p}}}}d\nu,

(B.19)

for all
(t,{\mathsf{p}})\in[{\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}},T]\times\mathbb{N}_{\geq 2}
.
Now, it follows from the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality that

\displaystyle\left\|R_{a}(\nu)\right\|_{L_{2{\mathsf{p}}}}=

\displaystyle\left\|L(\nu)\varsigma_{1}(\nu)\int_{(i^{\star}\left(\nu\right)-1){\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}}}^{i^{\star}\left(\nu\right){\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}}}e^{\theta_{2}\beta}\varsigma_{2}(\beta)dQ_{\beta}\right\|_{L_{2{\mathsf{p}}}}

\displaystyle\leq

\displaystyle\left\|L(\nu)\right\|_{L_{4{\mathsf{p}}}}\left|\varsigma_{1}(\nu)\right|\left\|\int_{(i^{\star}\left(\nu\right)-1){\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}}}^{i^{\star}\left(\nu\right){\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}}}e^{\theta_{2}\beta}\varsigma_{2}(\beta)dQ_{\beta}\right\|_{L_{4{\mathsf{p}}}},\quad\forall\nu\in[{\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}},t],

where we have used the fact that
\varsigma_{1}
is a deterministic function.
Using Lemma
B.2
to bound the Itô integral term, we get

\displaystyle\left\|R_{a}(\nu)\right\|_{L_{2{\mathsf{p}}}}

\displaystyle\leq\left({\mathsf{p}}(4{\mathsf{p}}-1)\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}e^{\theta_{2}i^{\star}\left(\nu\right){\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}}}\left(\frac{1-e^{-2\theta_{2}{\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}}}}{\theta_{2}}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\left\|L(\nu)\right\|_{L_{4{\mathsf{p}}}}\left|\varsigma_{1}(\nu)\right|\sup_{\beta\in[(i^{\star}\left(\nu\right)-1){\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}},i^{\star}\left(\nu\right){\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}}]}\left|\varsigma_{2}(\beta)\right|

\displaystyle\leq\left({\mathsf{p}}(4{\mathsf{p}}-1)\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}e^{\theta_{2}\nu}\left(\frac{1-e^{-2\theta_{2}{\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}}}}{\theta_{2}}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\left\|L(\nu)\right\|_{L_{4{\mathsf{p}}}}\left|\varsigma_{1}(\nu)\right|\sup_{\beta\in[(i^{\star}\left(\nu\right)-1){\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}},i^{\star}\left(\nu\right){\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}}]}\left|\varsigma_{2}(\beta)\right|,

(B.20)

for all
(t,{\mathsf{p}})\in[{\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}},T]\times\mathbb{N}_{\geq 2}
, where we have used the fact that
\varsigma_{2}
is a deterministic function. Further, the second inequality follows from
i^{\star}\left(\nu\right){\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}}\leq\nu
,
\forall\nu
.
Similarly, using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality and Lemma
B.2
:

\displaystyle\left\|R_{b}(\nu)\right\|_{L_{2{\mathsf{p}}}}\leq

\displaystyle\left({\mathsf{p}}(4{\mathsf{p}}-1)\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}e^{\theta_{2}\nu}\left(\frac{1-e^{2\theta_{2}(i^{\star}\left(\nu\right){\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}}-\nu)}}{\theta_{2}}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\left\|L(\nu)\right\|_{L_{4{\mathsf{p}}}}

\displaystyle\leq

\displaystyle\left({\mathsf{p}}(4{\mathsf{p}}-1)\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}e^{\theta_{2}\nu}\left(\frac{1-e^{-2\theta_{2}{\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}}}}{\theta_{2}}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\left\|L(\nu)\right\|_{L_{4{\mathsf{p}}}},\quad\forall(t,{\mathsf{p}})\in[{\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}},T]\times\mathbb{N}_{\geq 2},

(B.21)

where we obtain the second inequality by using the fact that
\nu-i^{\star}\left(\nu\right){\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}}\leq{\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}}
,
\forall\nu
.
Substituting (
B
) into (
B.19
) yields

\left\|N_{a}(t)\right\|_{L_{{\mathsf{p}}}}\leq\left({\mathsf{p}}(4{\mathsf{p}}-1)\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\left(\int_{{\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}}}^{t}e^{\theta_{1}\nu}d\nu\right)\left(\frac{1-e^{-2\theta_{2}{\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}}}}{\theta_{2}}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\
\times\sup_{\nu\in[{\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}},t]}\left[\left\|S(\nu)\right\|_{L_{2{\mathsf{p}}}}\left\|L(\nu)\right\|_{L_{4{\mathsf{p}}}}\left|\varsigma_{1}(\nu)\right|\sup_{\beta\in[(i^{\star}\left(\nu\right)-1){\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}},i^{\star}\left(\nu\right){\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}}]}\left|\varsigma_{2}(\beta)\right|\right],

for all
(t,{\mathsf{p}})\in[{\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}},T]\times\mathbb{N}_{\geq 2}
.
Solving the integral on the right hand side then leads to (
B.17
).
Substituting (
B
) into (
B.19
) and performing the same manipulations as above, we obtain (
B.18
).

∎

Next, we provide a converse result to Lemma
B.3
in which we derive a bound on a particular Itô integral with a Lebesgue integral in the integrand.

Lemma B.4

Given any
S\in\mathcal{M}_{2}^{loc}\left(\mathbb{R}^{n_{o}}|\mathfrak{F}_{t}\right)
,
L\in\mathcal{M}_{2}^{loc}\left(\mathbb{R}^{n_{o}\times n_{q}}|\mathfrak{F}_{t}\right)
,
\mathfrak{F}_{t}
-adapted Brownian motion
Q_{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{n_{q}}
, and strictly positive constants
\theta_{1},\,\theta_{2}\in\mathbb{R}_{>0}
, define

N(t)=\int_{0}^{t}e^{(\theta_{1}-\theta_{2})\nu}\left(\int_{0}^{\nu}e^{\theta_{2}\beta}S(\beta)d\beta\right)^{\top}L(\nu)dQ_{\nu}\in\mathbb{R},\quad t\in[0,T].

(B.22)

If

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\int_{0}^{T}\left(\left\|S(\nu)\right\|^{2{\mathsf{p}}}+\left\|L(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right)d\nu\right]<\infty,\quad\forall{\mathsf{p}}\geq 2,

then

\displaystyle\left\|N(t)\right\|_{L_{{\mathsf{p}}}}\leq\left({\mathsf{p}}({\mathsf{p}}-1)\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\frac{e^{\theta_{1}t}}{2\sqrt{\theta_{1}}\theta_{2}}\sup_{\nu\in[0,t]}\left\|S(\nu)\right\|_{L_{2{\mathsf{p}}}}\sup_{\nu\in[0,t]}\left\|L(\nu)\right\|_{L_{2{\mathsf{p}}}},\quad\forall(t,{\mathsf{p}})\in[0,T]\times\mathbb{N}_{\geq 2}.

(B.23)

Proof.

The proof for
{\mathsf{p}}=2
follows by using
[
91
, Thm. 1.5.21]
and following the proof for
{\mathsf{p}}>2

mutatis mutandis
, which we present below.
We begin by noting that the inner Lebesgue integral is absolute continuous on
[0,T]
by fundamental theorem for the Lebesgue integral
[
113
, Thm. 6.4.1]
, and
S\in\mathcal{M}_{2}^{loc}\left(\mathbb{R}^{n_{o}}|\mathfrak{F}_{t}\right)
implies that

\displaystyle\int_{0}^{t}e^{\theta_{2}\beta}S(\beta)d\beta\in\mathcal{M}_{2}^{loc}\left(\mathbb{R}^{n_{o}}|\mathfrak{F}_{t}\right).

It follows then from
[
90
, Thm. 5.5.2]
that
N(t)
is a continuous local martingale with respect to the filtration
\mathfrak{F}_{t}
since
L\in\mathcal{M}_{2}^{loc}\left(\mathbb{R}^{n_{o}\times n_{q}}|\mathfrak{F}_{t}\right)
.
Then, applying Itô’s lemma
[
91
, Thm. 1.6.4]
and using
[
91
, Thm. 1.5.21]
produces

\left|N(t)\right|^{\mathsf{p}}=\frac{{\mathsf{p}}}{2}\int_{0}^{t}e^{2(\theta_{1}-\theta_{2})\nu}\left|N(\nu)\right|^{{\mathsf{p}}-2}\left\|L(\nu)^{\top}\left(\int_{0}^{\nu}e^{\theta_{2}\beta}S(\beta)d\beta\right)\right\|^{2}d\nu\\
+\frac{{\mathsf{p}}}{2}({\mathsf{p}}-2)\int_{0}^{t}e^{2(\theta_{1}-\theta_{2})\nu}\left|N(\nu)\right|^{{\mathsf{p}}-4}\left\|N(\nu)L(\nu)^{\top}\left(\int_{0}^{\nu}e^{\theta_{2}\beta}S(\beta)d\beta\right)\right\|^{2}d\nu,

(B.24)

and therefore

\displaystyle\left|N(t)\right|^{\mathsf{p}}\leq\frac{{\mathsf{p}}}{2}({\mathsf{p}}-1)\int_{0}^{t}e^{2(\theta_{1}-\theta_{2})\nu}\left|N(\nu)\right|^{{\mathsf{p}}-2}\left\|L(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{2}\left\|\int_{0}^{\nu}e^{\theta_{2}\beta}S(\beta)d\beta\right\|^{2}d\nu,\quad\forall t\in[0,T].

Using this bound, we obtain

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left|N(t)\right|^{\mathsf{p}}\right]=

\displaystyle\frac{{\mathsf{p}}}{2}({\mathsf{p}}-1)\mathbb{E}\left[\int_{0}^{t}e^{2(\theta_{1}-\theta_{2})\nu}\left|N(\nu)\right|^{{\mathsf{p}}-2}\left\|L(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{2}\left\|\int_{0}^{\nu}e^{\theta_{2}\beta}S(\beta)d\beta\right\|^{2}d\nu\right]

\displaystyle\overset{(i)}{=}

\displaystyle\frac{{\mathsf{p}}}{2}({\mathsf{p}}-1)\mathbb{E}\left[\int_{0}^{t}\left(e^{2\theta_{1}({\mathsf{p}}-2)\nu/{\mathsf{p}}}\left|N(\nu)\right|^{{\mathsf{p}}-2}\right)\left(e^{2\left(2\theta_{1}/{\mathsf{p}}-\theta_{2}\right)\nu}\left\|L(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{2}\left\|\int_{0}^{\nu}e^{\theta_{2}\beta}S(\beta)d\beta\right\|^{2}\right)d\nu\right]

\displaystyle\overset{(ii)}{\leq}

\displaystyle\frac{{\mathsf{p}}}{2}({\mathsf{p}}-1)\mathbb{E}\left[\int_{0}^{t}e^{2\theta_{1}\nu}\left|N(\nu)\right|^{\mathsf{p}}d\nu\right]^{\frac{{\mathsf{p}}-2}{{\mathsf{p}}}}\mathbb{E}\left[\int_{0}^{t}e^{\left(2\theta_{1}-\theta_{2}{\mathsf{p}}\right)\nu}\left\|L(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{\mathsf{p}}\left\|\int_{0}^{\nu}e^{\theta_{2}\beta}S(\beta)d\beta\right\|^{\mathsf{p}}d\nu\right]^{\frac{2}{{\mathsf{p}}}},

for all
t\in[0,T]
, where we obtain
(i)
by writing

\displaystyle e^{2(\theta_{1}-\theta_{2})\nu}=e^{2\left[\theta_{1}\left(\frac{{\mathsf{p}}-2}{{\mathsf{p}}}+\frac{2}{{\mathsf{p}}}\right)-\theta_{2}\right]\nu}=e^{2\theta_{1}({\mathsf{p}}-2)\nu/{\mathsf{p}}}e^{2\left(2\theta_{1}/{\mathsf{p}}-\theta_{2}\right)\nu},

and
(ii)
follows from Hölder’s inequality with conjugates
{\mathsf{p}}/({\mathsf{p}}-2)
and
{\mathsf{p}}/2
.
Applying Fubini’s theorem, followed by the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality then leads to

\begin{aligned} \mathbb{E}\left[\left|N(t)\right|^{\mathsf{p}}\right]\leq&\frac{{\mathsf{p}}}{2}({\mathsf{p}}-1)\left(\int_{0}^{t}e^{2\theta_{1}\nu}\mathbb{E}\left[\left|N(\nu)\right|^{\mathsf{p}}\right]d\nu\right)^{\frac{{\mathsf{p}}-2}{{\mathsf{p}}}}\left(\int_{0}^{t}e^{\left(2\theta_{1}-\theta_{2}{\mathsf{p}}\right)\nu}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|L(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{\mathsf{p}}\left\|\int_{0}^{\nu}e^{\theta_{2}\beta}S(\beta)d\beta\right\|^{\mathsf{p}}\right]d\nu\right)^{\frac{2}{{\mathsf{p}}}}\\
\leq&\frac{{\mathsf{p}}}{2}({\mathsf{p}}-1)\left(\int_{0}^{t}e^{2\theta_{1}\nu}\mathbb{E}\left[\left|N(\nu)\right|^{\mathsf{p}}\right]d\nu\right)^{\frac{{\mathsf{p}}-2}{{\mathsf{p}}}}\end{aligned}\\
\times\left(\int_{0}^{t}e^{\left(2\theta_{1}-\theta_{2}{\mathsf{p}}\right)\nu}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|L(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{2}}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|\int_{0}^{\nu}e^{\theta_{2}\beta}S(\beta)d\beta\right\|^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{2}}d\nu\right)^{\frac{2}{{\mathsf{p}}}},

(B.25)

for all
t\in[0,T]
.

Using (
B.24
), one sees that
\mathbb{E}\left[\left|N(t)\right|^{\mathsf{p}}\right]
is non-decreasing over
t\in[0,T]
, and thus

\displaystyle\left(\int_{0}^{t}e^{2\theta_{1}\nu}\mathbb{E}\left[\left|N(\nu)\right|^{\mathsf{p}}\right]d\nu\right)^{\frac{{\mathsf{p}}-2}{{\mathsf{p}}}}\leq\left(\int_{0}^{t}e^{2\theta_{1}\nu}d\nu\right)^{\frac{{\mathsf{p}}-2}{{\mathsf{p}}}}\mathbb{E}\left[\left|N(t)\right|^{\mathsf{p}}\right]^{\frac{{\mathsf{p}}-2}{{\mathsf{p}}}},\quad\forall t\in[0,T].

(B.26)

Next, we use Proposition
B.1
for
\left\{\theta,\xi,n_{s}\right\}=\left\{\theta_{2},0,n_{o}\right\}
and obtain

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|\int_{0}^{\nu}e^{\theta_{2}\beta}S(\beta)d\beta\right\|^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{2}}\leq\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\int_{0}^{\nu}e^{\theta_{2}\beta}\left\|S(\beta)\right\|d\beta\right)^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{2}}\leq

\displaystyle\left(\frac{e^{\theta_{2}\nu}-1}{\theta_{2}}\right)^{\mathsf{p}}\sup_{\beta\in[0,\nu]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|S(\beta)\right\|^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{2}}

\displaystyle\leq

\displaystyle\frac{e^{\theta_{2}{\mathsf{p}}\nu}}{\theta_{2}^{\mathsf{p}}}\sup_{\beta\in[0,\nu]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|S(\beta)\right\|^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{2}},\quad\forall\nu\in[0,t],

where we have bounded
e^{\theta_{2}\nu}-1
by
e^{\theta_{2}\nu}
.
Therefore,

\left(\int_{0}^{t}e^{\left(2\theta_{1}-\theta_{2}{\mathsf{p}}\right)\nu}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|L(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{2}}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|\int_{0}^{\nu}e^{\theta_{2}\beta}S(\beta)d\beta\right\|^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{2}}d\nu\right)^{\frac{2}{{\mathsf{p}}}}\\
\leq\left(\frac{1}{\theta_{2}}\right)^{2}\left(\int_{0}^{t}e^{2\theta_{1}\nu}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|L(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{2}}\sup_{\beta\in[0,\nu]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|S(\beta)\right\|^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{2}}d\nu\right)^{\frac{2}{{\mathsf{p}}}}\\
\leq\left(\frac{1}{\theta_{2}}\right)^{2}\left(\int_{0}^{t}e^{2\theta_{1}\nu}d\nu\right)^{\frac{2}{{\mathsf{p}}}}\sup_{\nu\in[0,t]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|L(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{{\mathsf{p}}}}\sup_{\nu\in[0,t]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|S(\nu)\right\|^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{{\mathsf{p}}}},

(B.27)

for all
t\in[0,T]
.
Substituting (
B.26
) and (
B.27
) into (
B.25
) yields

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left|N(t)\right|^{\mathsf{p}}\right]\leq

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left|N(t)\right|^{\mathsf{p}}\right]^{\frac{{\mathsf{p}}-2}{{\mathsf{p}}}}{\mathsf{p}}\frac{({\mathsf{p}}-1)}{2}\frac{1}{\theta_{2}^{2}}\left(\int_{0}^{t}e^{2\theta_{1}\nu}d\nu\right)\sup_{\nu\in[0,t]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|L(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{{\mathsf{p}}}}\sup_{\nu\in[0,t]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|S(\nu)\right\|^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{{\mathsf{p}}}}

\displaystyle\leq

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left|N(t)\right|^{\mathsf{p}}\right]^{\frac{{\mathsf{p}}-2}{{\mathsf{p}}}}{\mathsf{p}}\frac{({\mathsf{p}}-1)}{4}\frac{e^{2\theta_{1}t}}{\theta_{1}\theta_{2}^{2}}\sup_{\nu\in[0,t]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|L(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{{\mathsf{p}}}}\sup_{\nu\in[0,t]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|S(\nu)\right\|^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{{\mathsf{p}}}},

for all
t\in[0,T]
, where we have bounded
e^{2\theta_{1}t}-1
by
e^{2\theta_{1}t}
.
This bound then implies that

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left|N(t)\right|^{\mathsf{p}}\right]^{\frac{2}{{\mathsf{p}}}}\leq

\displaystyle{\mathsf{p}}\frac{({\mathsf{p}}-1)}{4}\frac{e^{2\theta_{1}t}}{\theta_{1}\theta_{2}^{2}}\sup_{\nu\in[0,t]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|L(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{{\mathsf{p}}}}\sup_{\nu\in[0,t]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|S(\nu)\right\|^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{{\mathsf{p}}}},\quad\forall t\in[0,T],

thus establishing (
B.23
) for
{\mathsf{p}}>2
.

∎

We need the following corollary to the last result for Lemma
B.5
.

Corollary B.3

Consider a complete filtered probability space
\left(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P}\right)
with filtration
\mathfrak{F}_{t}
, and let
L_{1},\,L_{2}\in\mathcal{M}_{2}^{loc}\left(\mathbb{R}^{n_{l}\times n_{q}}|\mathfrak{F}_{t}\right)
satisfy

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\int_{0}^{T}\left\|L_{1}(\nu)+L_{2}(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{2{\mathsf{p}}}d\nu\right]<\infty,\quad\forall{\mathsf{p}}\geq 2.

Additionally, for any strictly positive constants
\theta_{1},\,\theta_{2}\in\mathbb{R}_{>0}
and an
\mathfrak{F}_{t}
-adapted Brownian motion
Q_{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{n_{q}}
define

\displaystyle\breve{N}(t)=\int_{0}^{t}e^{(\theta_{1}-\theta_{2})\nu}\left(\int_{0}^{\nu}e^{\theta_{2}\beta}L_{2}(\beta)dQ_{\beta}\right)^{\top}L_{1}(\nu)dQ_{\nu}\in\mathbb{R}.

Then,

\displaystyle\left\|\breve{N}(t)\right\|_{L_{{\mathsf{p}}}}\leq\frac{{\mathsf{p}}\sqrt{({\mathsf{p}}-1)(2{\mathsf{p}}-1)}}{2\sqrt{2}}\frac{e^{\theta_{1}t}}{\sqrt{\theta_{1}\theta_{2}}}\sup_{\nu\in[0,t]}\left\|L_{1}(\nu)\right\|_{L_{2{\mathsf{p}}}}\sup_{\nu\in[0,t]}\left\|L_{2}(\nu)\right\|_{L_{2{\mathsf{p}}}},\quad\forall(t,{\mathsf{p}})\in[0,T]\times\mathbb{N}_{\geq 2}.

(B.28)

Proof.

As in the proof of Lemma
B.4
, we provide a proof for
{\mathsf{p}}>2
only since the proof for
{\mathsf{p}}=2
follows
mutatis mutandis
by using
[
91
, Thm. 1.5.21]
.
For
{\mathsf{p}}>2
, applying Itô’s lemma
[
91
, Thm. 1.6.4]
and using
[
91
, Thm. 1.5.21]
produces

\left|\breve{N}(t)\right|^{\mathsf{p}}=\frac{{\mathsf{p}}}{2}\int_{0}^{t}e^{2(\theta_{1}-\theta_{2})\nu}\left|\breve{N}(\nu)\right|^{{\mathsf{p}}-2}\left\|L_{1}(\nu)^{\top}\left(\int_{0}^{\nu}e^{\theta_{2}\beta}L_{2}(\beta)dQ_{\beta}\right)\right\|^{2}d\nu\\
+\frac{{\mathsf{p}}}{2}({\mathsf{p}}-2)\int_{0}^{t}e^{2(\theta_{1}-\theta_{2})\nu}\left|\breve{N}(\nu)\right|^{{\mathsf{p}}-4}\left\|\breve{N}(\nu)L_{1}(\nu)^{\top}\left(\int_{0}^{\nu}e^{\theta_{2}\beta}L_{2}(\beta)dQ_{\beta}\right)\right\|^{2}d\nu,

(B.29)

and therefore

\displaystyle\left|\breve{N}(t)\right|^{\mathsf{p}}\leq\frac{{\mathsf{p}}}{2}({\mathsf{p}}-1)\int_{0}^{t}e^{2(\theta_{1}-\theta_{2})\nu}\left|\breve{N}(\nu)\right|^{{\mathsf{p}}-2}\left\|L_{1}(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{2}\left\|\int_{0}^{\nu}e^{\theta_{2}\beta}L_{2}(\beta)dQ_{\beta}\right\|^{2}d\nu,\quad\forall t\in[0,T].

Following the identical analysis that led to (
B.25
) in the proof of Lemma
B.4
, we obtain

\mathbb{E}\left[\left|\breve{N}(t)\right|^{\mathsf{p}}\right]\leq\frac{{\mathsf{p}}}{2}({\mathsf{p}}-1)\left(\int_{0}^{t}e^{2\theta_{1}\nu}\mathbb{E}\left[\left|\breve{N}(\nu)\right|^{\mathsf{p}}\right]d\nu\right)^{\frac{{\mathsf{p}}-2}{{\mathsf{p}}}}\\
\times\left(\int_{0}^{t}e^{\left(2\theta_{1}-\theta_{2}{\mathsf{p}}\right)\nu}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|L_{1}(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{2}}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|\int_{0}^{\nu}e^{\theta_{2}\beta}L_{2}(\beta)dQ_{\beta}\right\|^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{2}}d\nu\right)^{\frac{2}{{\mathsf{p}}}},

(B.30)

for all
t\in[0,T]
.
Using (
B.29
), one sees that
\mathbb{E}\left[\left|\breve{N}(t)\right|^{\mathsf{p}}\right]
is non-decreasing over
t\in[0,T]
, and thus

\displaystyle\left(\int_{0}^{t}e^{2\theta_{1}\nu}\mathbb{E}\left[\left|\breve{N}(\nu)\right|^{\mathsf{p}}\right]d\nu\right)^{\frac{{\mathsf{p}}-2}{{\mathsf{p}}}}\leq\left(\int_{0}^{t}e^{2\theta_{1}\nu}d\nu\right)^{\frac{{\mathsf{p}}-2}{{\mathsf{p}}}}\mathbb{E}\left[\left|\breve{N}(t)\right|^{\mathsf{p}}\right]^{\frac{{\mathsf{p}}-2}{{\mathsf{p}}}},\quad\forall t\in[0,T].

(B.31)

Next, we use Lemma
B.2
for
\left\{\theta,\xi\right\}=\left\{\theta_{2},0\right\}
and obtain

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|\int_{0}^{\nu}e^{\theta_{2}\beta}L_{2}(\beta)dQ_{\beta}\right\|^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{2}}\leq

\displaystyle\left({\mathsf{p}}\frac{2{\mathsf{p}}-1}{2}\right)^{\frac{{\mathsf{p}}}{2}}\left(\frac{e^{2\theta_{2}\nu}}{\theta_{2}}\right)^{\frac{{\mathsf{p}}}{2}}\sup_{\beta\in[0,\nu]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|L_{2}(\beta)\right\|_{F}^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{2}},\quad\forall\nu\in[0,t],

where we have bounded
e^{2\theta_{2}\nu}-1
by
e^{2\theta_{2}\nu}
.
Therefore,

\left(\int_{0}^{t}e^{\left(2\theta_{1}-\theta_{2}{\mathsf{p}}\right)\nu}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|L_{1}(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{2}}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|\int_{0}^{\nu}e^{\theta_{2}\beta}L_{2}(\beta)dQ_{\beta}\right\|^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{2}}d\nu\right)^{\frac{2}{{\mathsf{p}}}}\\
\leq{\mathsf{p}}\frac{2{\mathsf{p}}-1}{2\theta_{2}}\left(\int_{0}^{t}e^{2\theta_{1}\nu}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|L_{1}(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{2}}\sup_{\beta\in[0,\nu]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|L_{2}(\beta)\right\|_{F}^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{2}}d\nu\right)^{\frac{2}{{\mathsf{p}}}}\\
\leq{\mathsf{p}}\frac{2{\mathsf{p}}-1}{2\theta_{2}}\left(\int_{0}^{t}e^{2\theta_{1}\nu}d\nu\right)^{\frac{2}{{\mathsf{p}}}}\sup_{\nu\in[0,t]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|L_{1}(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{{\mathsf{p}}}}\sup_{\nu\in[0,t]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|L_{2}(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{{\mathsf{p}}}},

(B.32)

for all
t\in[0,T]
.
Substituting (
B.31
) and (
B.32
) into (
B.30
) yields

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left|\breve{N}(t)\right|^{\mathsf{p}}\right]\leq

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left|\breve{N}(t)\right|^{\mathsf{p}}\right]^{\frac{{\mathsf{p}}-2}{{\mathsf{p}}}}\frac{{\mathsf{p}}^{2}({\mathsf{p}}-1)(2{\mathsf{p}}-1)}{4\theta_{2}}\left(\int_{0}^{t}e^{2\theta_{1}\nu}d\nu\right)\sup_{\nu\in[0,t]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|L_{1}(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{{\mathsf{p}}}}\sup_{\nu\in[0,t]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|L_{2}(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{{\mathsf{p}}}}

\displaystyle\leq

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left|\breve{N}(t)\right|^{\mathsf{p}}\right]^{\frac{{\mathsf{p}}-2}{{\mathsf{p}}}}\frac{1}{8}{\mathsf{p}}^{2}({\mathsf{p}}-1)(2{\mathsf{p}}-1)\frac{e^{2\theta_{1}t}}{\theta_{1}\theta_{2}}\sup_{\nu\in[0,t]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|L_{1}(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{{\mathsf{p}}}}\sup_{\nu\in[0,t]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|L_{2}(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{{\mathsf{p}}}},

for all
t\in[0,T]
, where we have bounded
e^{2\theta_{1}t}-1
by
e^{2\theta_{1}t}
.
This bound then implies that

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left|\breve{N}(t)\right|^{\mathsf{p}}\right]^{\frac{2}{{\mathsf{p}}}}\leq\frac{1}{8}{\mathsf{p}}^{2}({\mathsf{p}}-1)(2{\mathsf{p}}-1)\frac{e^{2\theta_{1}t}}{\theta_{1}\theta_{2}}\sup_{\nu\in[0,t]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|L_{1}(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{{\mathsf{p}}}}\sup_{\nu\in[0,t]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|L_{2}(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{{\mathsf{p}}}},\quad\forall t\in[0,T],

thus establishing (
B.28
) for
{\mathsf{p}}>2
.

∎

The following result provides a bound on a class of nested Itô integrals.

Lemma B.5

Consider a complete filtered probability space
\left(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P}\right)
with filtration
\mathfrak{F}_{t}
, and let
L_{1},\,L_{2}\in\mathcal{M}_{2}^{loc}\left(\mathbb{R}^{n_{l}\times n_{q}}|\mathfrak{F}_{t}\right)
satisfy

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\int_{0}^{T}\left\|L_{1}(\nu)+L_{2}(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{2{\mathsf{p}}}d\nu\right]<\infty,\quad\forall{\mathsf{p}}\geq 2.

(B.33)

Additionally, for any strictly positive constants
\theta_{1},\,\theta_{2}\in\mathbb{R}_{>0}
and an
\mathfrak{F}_{t}
-adapted Brownian motion
Q_{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{n_{q}}
define

N(t)=\int_{0}^{t}e^{\theta_{2}\nu}\left(\int_{\nu}^{t}e^{(\theta_{1}-\theta_{2})\beta}L_{1}(\beta)dQ_{\beta}\right)^{\top}L_{2}(\nu)dQ_{\nu}\in\mathbb{R},\quad t\in[0,T].

Then,

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[N(t)\right]\leq

\displaystyle\sqrt{n_{l}}\frac{e^{\theta_{1}t}}{\theta_{1}}\sup_{\nu\in[0,t]}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|L_{1}(\nu)L_{2}(\nu)^{\top}\right\|_{F}\right],\quad\forall t\in[0,T],

(B.34)

and

\left\|N(t)\right\|_{L_{{\mathsf{p}}}}\leq\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left({\mathsf{p}}\frac{{\mathsf{p}}-1}{2}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\left({\mathsf{p}}\frac{2{\mathsf{p}}-1}{2}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\frac{e^{\theta_{1}t}}{\sqrt{\theta_{1}\theta_{2}}}\sup_{\nu\in[0,t]}\left\|L_{1}(\nu)\right\|_{L_{2{\mathsf{p}}}}\sup_{\nu\in[0,t]}\left\|L_{2}(\nu)\right\|_{L_{2{\mathsf{p}}}}\\
+\sqrt{n_{l}}\frac{e^{\theta_{1}t}}{\theta_{1}}\sup_{\nu\in[0,t]}\left\|L_{1}(\nu)L_{2}(\nu)^{\top}\right\|_{L_{{\mathsf{p}}}},

(B.35)

for all
(t,{\mathsf{p}})\in[0,T]\times\mathbb{N}_{\geq 2}
.

Proof.

We begin by setting

\displaystyle N_{1}(t)=\int_{0}^{t}e^{(\theta_{1}-\theta_{2})\nu}L_{1}(\nu)dQ_{\nu}\in\mathbb{R}^{n_{l}},\quad N_{2}(t)=\int_{0}^{t}e^{\theta_{2}\nu}L_{2}(\nu)dQ_{\nu}\in\mathbb{R}^{n_{l}},\quad t\in[0,T].

It then follows from the definition of
N(t)
that

\displaystyle N(t)=\int_{0}^{t}e^{\theta_{2}\nu}\left(\int_{\nu}^{t}e^{(\theta_{1}-\theta_{2})\beta}L_{1}(\beta)dQ_{\beta}\right)^{\top}L_{2}(\nu)dQ_{\nu}=

\displaystyle\int_{0}^{t}\left(\int_{\nu}^{t}dN_{1}(\beta)\right)^{\top}dN_{2}(\nu).

Hence,

N(t)=\int_{0}^{t}\left(\int_{0}^{t}dN_{1}(\beta)\right)^{\top}dN_{2}(\nu)-\int_{0}^{t}\left(\int_{0}^{\nu}dN_{1}(\beta)\right)^{\top}dN_{2}(\nu)\\
=N_{1}(t)^{\top}N_{2}(t)-\int_{0}^{t}N_{1}(\nu)^{\top}dN_{2}(\nu),\quad t\in[0,T].

(B.36)

Next, applying Itô’s lemma to
N_{1}(t)^{\top}N_{2}(t)
(or alternatively using the Itô product rule
[
107
, Sec. 4.4.2]
applied element wise) produces

\displaystyle N_{1}(t)^{\top}N_{2}(t)=\int_{0}^{t}N_{1}(\nu)^{\top}dN_{2}(\nu)+\int_{0}^{t}N_{2}(\nu)^{\top}dN_{1}(\nu)+\sum_{i=1}^{n_{l}}\Bigl\langle N_{1,i},N_{2,i}\Bigr\rangle_{t},\quad t\in[0,T],

where
N_{1,i},\,N_{2,i}\in\mathbb{R}
denote the
i^{th}
scalar-valued process,
i\in\left\{1,\dots,n_{l}\right\}
, of
N_{1}(t)
and
N_{2}(t)
, respectively, and
\Bigl\langle N_{1,i},N_{2,i}\Bigr\rangle_{t}
denotes the cross-variation process between
N_{1,i}(t)
and
N_{2,i}(t)

[
89
, Defn. 2.3.9]
.
Substituting the above expression for
N_{1}(t)^{\top}N_{2}(t)
into (
B.36
) produces

\displaystyle N(t)=

\displaystyle\int_{0}^{t}N_{2}(\nu)^{\top}dN_{1}(\nu)+\sum_{i=1}^{n_{l}}\Bigl\langle N_{1,i},N_{2,i}\Bigr\rangle_{t},\quad t\in[0,T].

It then follows from the linearity of the expectation operator and the Minkowski’s inequality that

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[N(t)\right]=

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\int_{0}^{t}N_{2}(\nu)^{\top}dN_{1}(\nu)\right]+\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{i=1}^{n_{l}}\Bigl\langle N_{1,i},N_{2,i}\Bigr\rangle_{t}\right]

\displaystyle\leq

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\int_{0}^{t}N_{2}(\nu)^{\top}dN_{1}(\nu)\right]+\mathbb{E}\left[\left|\sum_{i=1}^{n_{l}}\Bigl\langle N_{1,i},N_{2,i}\Bigr\rangle_{t}\right|\right],\quad\forall t\in[0,T],

(B.37)

and

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left|N(t)\right|^{\mathsf{p}}\right]^{\frac{1}{{\mathsf{p}}}}\leq\mathbb{E}\left[\left|\int_{0}^{t}N_{2}(\nu)^{\top}dN_{1}(\nu)\right|^{\mathsf{p}}\right]^{\frac{1}{{\mathsf{p}}}}+\mathbb{E}\left[\left|\sum_{i=1}^{n_{l}}\Bigl\langle N_{1,i},N_{2,i}\Bigr\rangle_{t}\right|^{\mathsf{p}}\right]^{\frac{1}{{\mathsf{p}}}},\quad\forall(t,{\mathsf{p}})\in[0,T]\times\mathbb{N}_{\geq 2}.

(B.38)

Now, let

\displaystyle\breve{N}(t)\doteq\int_{0}^{t}N_{2}(\nu)^{\top}dN_{1}(\nu)=\int_{0}^{t}e^{(\theta_{1}-\theta_{2})\nu}\left(\int_{0}^{\nu}e^{\theta_{2}\beta}L_{2}(\beta)dQ_{\beta}\right)^{\top}L_{1}(\nu)dQ_{\nu}\in\mathbb{R}.

The
t
-continuity of
N_{2}(t)

[
15
, Thm. 3.2.5]
, along with
L_{1},\,L_{2}\in\mathcal{M}_{2}^{loc}\left(\mathbb{R}^{n_{l}\times n_{q}}|\mathfrak{F}_{t}\right)
imply that
\breve{N}(t)
is a continuous local martingale
[
90
, Thm. 5.5.2]
.
Hence, it follows from
[
91
, Thm. 1.5.21]
that

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\breve{N}(t)\right]=\mathbb{E}\left[\int_{0}^{t}N_{2}(\nu)^{\top}dN_{1}(\nu)\right]=0,\quad\forall t\in[0,T].

(B.39)

Furthermore, from Corollary
B.3
, we have that

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left|\breve{N}(t)\right|^{\mathsf{p}}\right]^{\frac{1}{{\mathsf{p}}}}=

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left|\int_{0}^{t}N_{2}(\nu)^{\top}dN_{1}(\nu)\right|^{\mathsf{p}}\right]^{\frac{1}{{\mathsf{p}}}}

\displaystyle\leq

\displaystyle\frac{{\mathsf{p}}\sqrt{({\mathsf{p}}-1)(2{\mathsf{p}}-1)}}{2\sqrt{2}}\frac{e^{\theta_{1}t}}{\sqrt{\theta_{1}\theta_{2}}}\sup_{\nu\in[0,t]}\left\|L_{1}(\nu)\right\|_{L_{2{\mathsf{p}}}}\sup_{\nu\in[0,t]}\left\|L_{2}(\nu)\right\|_{L_{2{\mathsf{p}}}},

(B.40)

for all
(t,{\mathsf{p}})\in[0,T]\times\mathbb{N}_{\geq 2}
.

Next, it follows from the definition of the cross-variation process
[
89
, Defn. 2.3.9]
that

\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{n_{l}}\Bigl\langle N_{1,i},N_{2,i}\Bigr\rangle_{t}=\frac{1}{4}\sum_{i=1}^{n_{l}}\left(\Bigl\langle N_{1,i}+N_{2,i}\Bigr\rangle_{t}-\Bigl\langle N_{1,i}-N_{2,i}\Bigr\rangle_{t}\right)=\sum_{i=1}^{n_{l}}\int_{0}^{t}e^{\theta_{1}\nu}L_{1,i}(\nu)L_{2,i}(\nu)^{\top}d\nu,

where
L_{1,i},\,L_{2,i}\in\mathbb{R}^{1\times n_{q}}
denote the
i^{th}
rows of
L_{1}(t)
and
L_{2}(t)
, respectively.
Hence,

\displaystyle\left|\sum_{i=1}^{n_{l}}\Bigl\langle N_{1,i},N_{2,i}\Bigr\rangle_{t}\right|\leq\int_{0}^{t}e^{\theta_{1}\nu}\left|\sum_{i=1}^{n_{l}}L_{1,i}(\nu)L_{2,i}(\nu)^{\top}\right|d\nu\leq

\displaystyle\sqrt{n_{l}}\int_{0}^{t}e^{\theta_{1}\nu}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n_{l}}\left|L_{1,i}(\nu)L_{2,i}(\nu)^{\top}\right|^{2}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}d\nu

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\sqrt{n_{l}}\int_{0}^{t}e^{\theta_{1}\nu}\left\|L_{1}(\nu)L_{2}(\nu)^{\top}\right\|_{F}d\nu,

for all
t\in[0,T]
.
Then, applying Proposition
B.1
for
\left\{\theta,\xi,\left\|S(t)\right\|\right\}=\left\{\theta_{1},0,\left\|L_{1}(t)L_{2}(t)^{\top}\right\|_{F}\right\}
leads to

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left|\sum_{i=1}^{m}\Bigl\langle N_{1,i},N_{2,i}\Bigr\rangle_{t}\right|^{\mathsf{p}}\right]^{\frac{1}{{\mathsf{p}}}}\leq\sqrt{n_{l}}\frac{e^{\theta_{1}t}}{\theta_{1}}\sup_{\nu\in[0,t]}\left\|L_{1}(\nu)L_{2}(\nu)^{\top}\right\|_{L_{{\mathsf{p}}}},\quad\forall(t,{\mathsf{p}})\in[0,T]\times\mathbb{N}_{\geq 1},

(B.41)

where we have bounded
e^{\theta_{1}t}-1
by
e^{\theta_{1}t}
.
Substituting (
B.39
), (
B
), and (
B.41
) into (
B
) and (
B.38
) produces the desired result.

∎

The final major result of this section provides a bound on a class of nested Itô and Lebesgue integrals.

Lemma B.6

Consider a complete filtered probability space
\left(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P}\right)
with filtration
\mathfrak{F}_{t}
, and let
R\in\mathcal{M}_{2}^{loc}\left(\mathbb{R}^{n_{1}\times n_{2}}|\mathfrak{F}_{t}\right)
,
S_{1}\in\mathcal{M}_{2}^{loc}\left(\mathbb{R}^{n_{1}}|\mathfrak{F}_{t}\right)
,
S_{2}\in\mathcal{M}_{2}^{loc}\left(\mathbb{R}^{n_{2}}|\mathfrak{F}_{t}\right)
,
L_{1}\in\mathcal{M}_{2}^{loc}\left(\mathbb{R}^{n_{1}\times n_{q}}|\mathfrak{F}_{t}\right)
, and
L_{2}\in\mathcal{M}_{2}^{loc}\left(\mathbb{R}^{n_{2}\times n_{q}}|\mathfrak{F}_{t}\right)
satisfy

\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{2}\mathbb{E}\left[\int_{0}^{T}\left(\left\|R(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{2{\mathsf{p}}}+\left\|S_{i}(\nu)\right\|^{2{\mathsf{p}}}+\left\|L_{i}(\nu)\right\|_{F}^{2{\mathsf{p}}}\right)d\nu\right]<\infty,\quad\forall{\mathsf{p}}\geq 1.

Additionally, for any constants
\theta_{1},\,\theta_{2}\in\mathbb{R}_{>0}
and an
\mathfrak{F}_{t}
-adapted Brownian motion
Q_{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{n_{q}}
define

N(t)=\int_{\xi}^{t}e^{2(\theta_{1}-\theta_{2})\nu}\mathchoice{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.81778pt$\hss\resizebox{6.13614pt}{3.8889pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\displaystyle R\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.81778pt$\hss\resizebox{6.13614pt}{3.8889pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\textstyle R\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.81778pt$\hss\resizebox{4.84808pt}{3.12502pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\scriptstyle R\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.81778pt$\hss\resizebox{4.12645pt}{2.70836pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\scriptscriptstyle R\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}_{1}(\nu)^{\top}R(\nu)\mathchoice{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.81778pt$\hss\resizebox{6.13614pt}{3.8889pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\displaystyle R\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.81778pt$\hss\resizebox{6.13614pt}{3.8889pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\textstyle R\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.81778pt$\hss\resizebox{4.84808pt}{3.12502pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\scriptstyle R\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.81778pt$\hss\resizebox{4.12645pt}{2.70836pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\scriptscriptstyle R\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}_{2}(\nu)d\nu\in\mathbb{R},\quad 0\leq\xi\leq t\leq T,

(B.42)

where
\xi\in\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}
is a constant, and

\displaystyle\mathchoice{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.81778pt$\hss\resizebox{6.13614pt}{3.8889pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\displaystyle R\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.81778pt$\hss\resizebox{6.13614pt}{3.8889pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\textstyle R\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.81778pt$\hss\resizebox{4.84808pt}{3.12502pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\scriptstyle R\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.81778pt$\hss\resizebox{4.12645pt}{2.70836pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\scriptscriptstyle R\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}_{1}(t)=\int_{0}^{t}e^{\theta_{2}\beta}\left[S_{1}(\beta)d\beta+L_{1}(\beta)dQ_{\beta}\right]\in\mathbb{R}^{n_{1}},\quad\mathchoice{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.81778pt$\hss\resizebox{6.13614pt}{3.8889pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\displaystyle R\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.81778pt$\hss\resizebox{6.13614pt}{3.8889pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\textstyle R\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.81778pt$\hss\resizebox{4.84808pt}{3.12502pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\scriptstyle R\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.81778pt$\hss\resizebox{4.12645pt}{2.70836pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\scriptscriptstyle R\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}_{2}(t)=\int_{0}^{t}e^{\theta_{2}\beta}\left[S_{2}(\beta)d\beta+L_{2}(\beta)dQ_{\beta}\right]\in\mathbb{R}^{n_{2}}.

If there exists a constant
\Delta_{R}\in\mathbb{R}_{>0}
such that

\displaystyle\left\|R(t)\right\|_{F}\leq\Delta_{R},\quad\forall t\in[0,T],

then, the following bound holds for all
(t,{\mathsf{p}})\in[\xi,T]\times\mathbb{N}_{\geq 1}
:

\left\|N(t)\right\|_{L_{{\mathsf{p}}}}\leq\Delta_{R}\frac{e^{2\theta_{1}t}-e^{2\theta_{1}\xi}}{2\theta_{1}}\prod_{i=1}^{2}\left(\frac{1-e^{-\theta_{2}t}}{\theta_{2}}\sup_{\nu\in[0,t]}\left\|S_{i}(\nu)\right\|_{L_{2{\mathsf{p}}}}\right.\\
\left.+\left({\mathsf{p}}\frac{2{\mathsf{p}}-1}{2}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\left(\frac{1-e^{-2\theta_{2}t}}{\theta_{2}}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\sup_{\nu\in[0,t]}\left\|L_{i}(\nu)\right\|_{L_{2{\mathsf{p}}}}\right).

(B.43)

Proof.

We begin with the case
{\mathsf{p}}=1
by observing that one has the straightforward bound

\displaystyle\left|N(t)\right|\leq\Delta_{R}\int_{\xi}^{t}e^{2(\theta_{1}-\theta_{2})\nu}\left\|\mathchoice{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.80002pt$\hss\resizebox{6.13614pt}{3.8889pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\displaystyle R\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.80002pt$\hss\resizebox{6.13614pt}{3.8889pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\textstyle R\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.80002pt$\hss\resizebox{4.84808pt}{3.12502pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\scriptstyle R\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.80002pt$\hss\resizebox{4.12645pt}{2.70836pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\scriptscriptstyle R\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}_{1}(\nu)\right\|\left\|\mathchoice{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.80002pt$\hss\resizebox{6.13614pt}{3.8889pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\displaystyle R\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.80002pt$\hss\resizebox{6.13614pt}{3.8889pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\textstyle R\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.80002pt$\hss\resizebox{4.84808pt}{3.12502pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\scriptstyle R\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.80002pt$\hss\resizebox{4.12645pt}{2.70836pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\scriptscriptstyle R\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}_{2}(\nu)\right\|d\nu,\quad\forall t\in[\xi,T].

Applying Fubini’s theorem, followed by the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality produces

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left|N(t)\right|\right]\leq\Delta_{R}\int_{\xi}^{t}e^{2(\theta_{1}-\theta_{2})\nu}\left\|\mathchoice{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.80002pt$\hss\resizebox{6.13614pt}{3.8889pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\displaystyle R\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.80002pt$\hss\resizebox{6.13614pt}{3.8889pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\textstyle R\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.80002pt$\hss\resizebox{4.84808pt}{3.12502pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\scriptstyle R\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.80002pt$\hss\resizebox{4.12645pt}{2.70836pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\scriptscriptstyle R\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}_{1}(\nu)\right\|_{L_{2}}\left\|\mathchoice{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.80002pt$\hss\resizebox{6.13614pt}{3.8889pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\displaystyle R\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.80002pt$\hss\resizebox{6.13614pt}{3.8889pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\textstyle R\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.80002pt$\hss\resizebox{4.84808pt}{3.12502pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\scriptstyle R\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.80002pt$\hss\resizebox{4.12645pt}{2.70836pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\scriptscriptstyle R\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}_{2}(\nu)\right\|_{L_{2}}d\nu,\quad\forall t\in[\xi,T].

(B.60)

Using the Minkowski’s inequality, one can establish that

\displaystyle\left\|\mathchoice{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.80002pt$\hss\resizebox{6.13614pt}{3.8889pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\displaystyle R\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.80002pt$\hss\resizebox{6.13614pt}{3.8889pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\textstyle R\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.80002pt$\hss\resizebox{4.84808pt}{3.12502pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\scriptstyle R\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.80002pt$\hss\resizebox{4.12645pt}{2.70836pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\scriptscriptstyle R\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}_{i}(\nu)\right\|_{L_{2}}\leq\left\|\int_{0}^{\nu}e^{\theta_{2}\beta}\left\|S_{i}(\beta)d\beta\right\|\right\|_{L_{2}}+\left\|\int_{0}^{\nu}e^{\theta_{2}\beta}L_{i}(\beta)dQ_{\beta}\right\|_{L_{2}},\quad\forall(\nu,i)\in[\xi,t]\times\left\{1,2\right\}.

Using Proposition
B.1
and Lemma
B.2
, we obtain

\displaystyle\left\|\mathchoice{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.80002pt$\hss\resizebox{6.13614pt}{3.8889pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\displaystyle R\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.80002pt$\hss\resizebox{6.13614pt}{3.8889pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\textstyle R\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.80002pt$\hss\resizebox{4.84808pt}{3.12502pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\scriptstyle R\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.80002pt$\hss\resizebox{4.12645pt}{2.70836pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\scriptscriptstyle R\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}_{i}(\nu)\right\|_{L_{2}}\leq e^{\theta_{2}\nu}\left(\frac{1-e^{-\theta_{2}\nu}}{\theta_{2}}\sup_{\beta\in[0,\nu]}\left\|S_{i}(\beta)\right\|_{L_{2}}+\left(\frac{1-e^{-2\theta_{2}\nu}}{2\theta_{2}}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\sup_{\beta\in[0,\nu]}\left\|L_{i}(\beta)\right\|_{L_{2}}\right),

for all
(\nu,i)\in[\xi,t]\times\left\{1,2\right\}
.
Substituting the above inequality into (
B.60
) leads to

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left|N(t)\right|\right]\leq\Delta_{R}\int_{\xi}^{t}e^{2\theta_{1}\nu}\prod_{i=1}^{2}\left(\frac{1-e^{-\theta_{2}\nu}}{\theta_{2}}\sup_{\beta\in[0,\nu]}\left\|S_{i}(\beta)\right\|_{L_{2}}+\left(\frac{1-e^{-2\theta_{2}\nu}}{2\theta_{2}}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\sup_{\beta\in[0,\nu]}\left\|L_{i}(\beta)\right\|_{L_{2}}\right)d\nu,

which can be further developed into

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left|N(t)\right|\right]\leq\Delta_{R}\left(\int_{\xi}^{t}e^{2\theta_{1}\nu}d\nu\right)\prod_{i=1}^{2}\left(\frac{1-e^{-\theta_{2}t}}{\theta_{2}}\sup_{\nu\in[0,t]}\left\|S_{i}(\nu)\right\|_{L_{2}}+\left(\frac{1-e^{-2\theta_{2}t}}{2\theta_{2}}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\sup_{\nu\in[0,t]}\left\|L_{i}(\nu)\right\|_{L_{2}}\right),

for all
t\in[\xi,T]
.
Solving the integral on the right hand side of the above inequality produces the desired result for
{\mathsf{p}}=1
.

Next, consider
{\mathsf{p}}\in\mathbb{N}_{\geq 2}
, and define

\displaystyle\mathchoice{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.80002pt$\hss\resizebox{7.3pt}{3.8889pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\displaystyle N\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.80002pt$\hss\resizebox{7.3pt}{3.8889pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\textstyle N\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.80002pt$\hss\resizebox{5.6678pt}{3.12502pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\scriptstyle N\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.80002pt$\hss\resizebox{4.73894pt}{2.70836pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\scriptscriptstyle N\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}(t)=\int_{\xi}^{t}e^{2(\theta_{1}-\theta_{2})\nu}\left\|\mathchoice{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.80002pt$\hss\resizebox{6.13614pt}{3.8889pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\displaystyle R\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.80002pt$\hss\resizebox{6.13614pt}{3.8889pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\textstyle R\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern 0.80002pt$\hss\resizebox{4.84808pt}{3.12502pt}{\rotatebox[origin={c}]{90.0}{(}}\hss$\crcr\cr$\hss\scriptstyle R\hss$\crcr}}}\limits}{\mathop{\vbox{\halign{#\cr\kern
