(C.51)

and

\begin{aligned} &\left\|e^{-(2\lambda+{\color[rgb]{1,0,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{1,0,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0}{1}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0}{1}{0}{0}\bm{\omega}})\tau(t)}\Xi^{r}_{\mathcal{U}}\left(\tau(t),Y_{N};{\color[rgb]{1,0,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{1,0,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0}{1}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0}{1}{0}{0}\bm{\omega}}\right)\right\|_{L_{\mathsf{p}}}^{y_{0}}\\

(C.53)

Using the definition of

\displaystyle\int_{0}^{t}e^{{\color[rgb]{1,0,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{1,0,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0}{1}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0}{1}{0}{0}\bm{\omega}}\nu}\mathcal{P}^{r}_{\circ}\left(t,\nu\right)\left[\Lambda_{\mu}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.4pt}{\resizebox{5.91821pt}{6.29999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.4pt}{\resizebox{5.91821pt}{6.29999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.98pt}{\resizebox{4.27098pt}{4.40999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.7pt}{\resizebox{3.57098pt}{3.15pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\parallel$}}}}}}\left(\nu,X^{r}_{N,\nu}\right)d\nu+F^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.4pt}{\resizebox{5.91821pt}{6.29999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.4pt}{\resizebox{5.91821pt}{6.29999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.98pt}{\resizebox{4.27098pt}{4.40999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.7pt}{\resizebox{3.57098pt}{3.15pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\parallel$}}}}}}_{\sigma}\left(\nu,X^{r}_{N,\nu}\right)dW_{\nu}\right]=\sum_{i=1}^{4}N^{r}_{i}(t),\quad\forall t\in[0,T],

Hence, we may write (

\displaystyle dZ_{N,t}=

(D.23)

\displaystyle\mathring{\Lambda}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.4pt}{\resizebox{5.91821pt}{6.29999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.4pt}{\resizebox{5.91821pt}{6.29999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.98pt}{\resizebox{4.27098pt}{4.40999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.7pt}{\resizebox{3.57098pt}{3.15pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\parallel$}}}}}}_{\mu}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)=\Lambda_{\mu}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.4pt}{\resizebox{5.91821pt}{6.29999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.4pt}{\resizebox{5.91821pt}{6.29999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.98pt}{\resizebox{4.27098pt}{4.40999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.7pt}{\resizebox{3.57098pt}{3.15pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\parallel$}}}}}}\left(\nu,X_{N,\nu}\right)-\Lambda_{\mu}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.4pt}{\resizebox{5.91821pt}{6.29999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.4pt}{\resizebox{5.91821pt}{6.29999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.98pt}{\resizebox{4.27098pt}{4.40999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.7pt}{\resizebox{3.57098pt}{3.15pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\parallel$}}}}}}\left(\nu,X^{r}_{N,\nu}\right),\quad\mathring{F}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.4pt}{\resizebox{5.91821pt}{6.29999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.4pt}{\resizebox{5.91821pt}{6.29999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.98pt}{\resizebox{4.27098pt}{4.40999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.7pt}{\resizebox{3.57098pt}{3.15pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\parallel$}}}}}}_{\sigma}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)=F^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.4pt}{\resizebox{5.91821pt}{6.29999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.4pt}{\resizebox{5.91821pt}{6.29999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.98pt}{\resizebox{4.27098pt}{4.40999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.7pt}{\resizebox{3.57098pt}{3.15pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\parallel$}}}}}}_{\sigma}\left(\nu,X_{N,\nu}\right)-F^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.4pt}{\resizebox{5.91821pt}{6.29999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.4pt}{\resizebox{5.91821pt}{6.29999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.98pt}{\resizebox{4.27098pt}{4.40999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.7pt}{\resizebox{3.57098pt}{3.15pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\parallel$}}}}}}_{\sigma}\left(\nu,X^{r}_{N,\nu}\right),

\displaystyle\mathring{\mathcal{F}}_{r}\left(Z_{N}\right)(\nu)=\mathcal{F}_{r}\left(X_{N}\right)(\nu)-\mathcal{F}_{r}\left(X^{r}_{N}\right)(\nu).

Proof.

Using the definitions of
J_{\mu}
in (
97
) and the decomposition of
F_{\mu}
in (
3
), we have that

\displaystyle\nabla\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\nu}\right)^{\top}J_{\mu}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)=

\displaystyle 2\left(X_{N,\nu}-X^{r}_{N,\nu}\right)^{\top}\left(F_{\mu}\left(\nu,X_{N,\nu},U_{\mathcal{L}_{1},\nu}\right)-F_{\mu}\left(\nu,X^{r}_{N,\nu},U^{r}_{\nu}\right)\right)

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle 2\left(X_{N,\nu}-X^{r}_{N,\nu}\right)^{\top}\left(\bar{F}_{\mu}\left(\nu,X_{N,\nu}\right)-\bar{F}_{\mu}\left(\nu,X^{r}_{N,\nu}\right)\right)

\displaystyle+2\left(X_{N,\nu}-X^{r}_{N,\nu}\right)^{\top}\left[g(\nu)\left(U_{\mathcal{L}_{1},\nu}-U^{r}_{\nu}\right)+\Lambda_{\mu}\left(\nu,X_{N,\nu}\right)-\Lambda_{\mu}\left(\nu,X^{r}_{N,\nu}\right)\right],

for all
\nu\in[0,\tau(t)]
, which, due to Lemma
2.1
reduces to

\nabla\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\nu}\right)^{\top}J_{\mu}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)\leq-2\lambda\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\nu}\right)+\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\nu}\right)^{\top}g(\nu)\left(U_{\mathcal{L}_{1},\nu}-U^{r}_{\nu}\right)\\
+\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\nu}\right)^{\top}\left(\Lambda_{\mu}\left(\nu,X_{N,\nu}\right)-\Lambda_{\mu}\left(\nu,X^{r}_{N,\nu}\right)\right),

(D.25)

for all
\nu\in[0,\tau(t)]
, where we have used the definition
\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\nu}\right)=2\left(X_{N,\nu}-X^{r}_{N,\nu}\right)
.
We develop the expression further by using (
7
) in Assumption
4
to conclude that

\displaystyle\Lambda_{\mu}\left(\nu,\cdot\right)=\begin{bmatrix}g(\nu)&g(\nu)^{\perp}\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}\Lambda_{\mu}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.4pt}{\resizebox{5.91821pt}{6.29999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.4pt}{\resizebox{5.91821pt}{6.29999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.98pt}{\resizebox{4.27098pt}{4.40999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.7pt}{\resizebox{3.57098pt}{3.15pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\parallel$}}}}}}\left(\nu,\cdot\right)\\
\Lambda_{\mu}^{\perp}\left(\nu,\cdot\right)\end{bmatrix}=g(\nu)\Lambda_{\mu}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.4pt}{\resizebox{5.91821pt}{6.29999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.4pt}{\resizebox{5.91821pt}{6.29999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.98pt}{\resizebox{4.27098pt}{4.40999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.7pt}{\resizebox{3.57098pt}{3.15pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\parallel$}}}}}}\left(\nu,\cdot\right)+g(\nu)^{\perp}\Lambda_{\mu}^{\perp}\left(\nu,\cdot\right),

which allows us to write (
D.25
) as

\nabla\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\nu}\right)^{\top}J_{\mu}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)\leq-2\lambda\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\nu}\right)+\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\nu}\right)^{\top}g(\nu)\left(U_{\mathcal{L}_{1},\nu}-U^{r}_{\nu}\right)\\
+\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\nu}\right)^{\top}g(\nu)\left(\Lambda_{\mu}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.4pt}{\resizebox{5.91821pt}{6.29999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.4pt}{\resizebox{5.91821pt}{6.29999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.98pt}{\resizebox{4.27098pt}{4.40999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.7pt}{\resizebox{3.57098pt}{3.15pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\parallel$}}}}}}\left(\nu,X_{N,\nu}\right)-\Lambda_{\mu}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.4pt}{\resizebox{5.91821pt}{6.29999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.4pt}{\resizebox{5.91821pt}{6.29999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.98pt}{\resizebox{4.27098pt}{4.40999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.7pt}{\resizebox{3.57098pt}{3.15pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\parallel$}}}}}}\left(\nu,X^{r}_{N,\nu}\right)\right)\\
+\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\nu}\right)^{\top}g(\nu)^{\perp}\left(\Lambda_{\mu}^{\perp}\left(\nu,X_{N,\nu}\right)-\Lambda_{\mu}^{\perp}\left(\nu,X^{r}_{N,\nu}\right)\right),\quad\forall\nu\in[0,\tau(t)].

(D.26)

For the truncated processes
X_{N,t}
and
X^{r}_{N,t}
, we have from (
27
) and (
91
) that

\displaystyle U^{r}_{t}=\mathcal{F}_{r}\left(X^{r}_{N}\right)(t),\quad U_{\mathcal{L}_{1},t}=\mathcal{F}_{\mathcal{L}_{1}}\left(X_{N}\right)\left(t\right).

Thus, by adding and subtracting
\mathcal{F}_{r}\left(X_{N}\right)(t)
, we obtain

\displaystyle U_{\mathcal{L}_{1},t}-U^{r}_{t}=\mathcal{F}_{\mathcal{L}_{1}}\left(X_{N}\right)\left(t\right)-\mathcal{F}_{r}\left(X^{r}_{N}\right)(t)=

\displaystyle\left[\mathcal{F}_{\mathcal{L}_{1}}\left(X_{N}\right)\left(t\right)-\mathcal{F}_{r}\left(X_{N}\right)(t)\right]-\mathcal{F}_{r}\left(X^{r}_{N}\right)(t)+\mathcal{F}_{r}\left(X_{N}\right)(t)

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\left(\mathcal{F}_{\mathcal{L}_{1}}-\mathcal{F}_{r}\right)\left(X_{N}\right)(t)+\mathring{\mathcal{F}}_{r}\left(Z_{N}\right)(\nu).

(D.27)

Substituting into (
D.26
) yields

\nabla\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\nu}\right)^{\top}J_{\mu}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)\leq-2\lambda\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\nu}\right)+\widetilde{\mathcal{U}}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)+\phi_{U}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)+\phi_{\mu^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\resizebox{5.31639pt}{4.5pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\displaystyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\resizebox{5.31639pt}{4.5pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\textstyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.7pt}{\resizebox{3.3858pt}{3.15pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptstyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.5pt}{\resizebox{2.8858pt}{2.25pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.625pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\parallel$}}}}}}}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)\\
+\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\nu}\right)^{\top}g(\nu)^{\perp}\left(\Lambda_{\mu}^{\perp}\left(\nu,X_{N,\nu}\right)-\Lambda_{\mu}^{\perp}\left(\nu,X^{r}_{N,\nu}\right)\right),

(D.28)

for all
\nu\in[0,\tau(t)]
, where

\displaystyle\phi_{\mu^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\resizebox{5.31639pt}{4.5pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\displaystyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.0pt}{\resizebox{5.31639pt}{4.5pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.25pt}{$\textstyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.7pt}{\resizebox{3.3858pt}{3.15pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptstyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.5pt}{\resizebox{2.8858pt}{2.25pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.625pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\parallel$}}}}}}}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)=\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\nu}\right)^{\top}g(\nu)\left[\Lambda_{\mu}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.4pt}{\resizebox{5.91821pt}{6.29999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.4pt}{\resizebox{5.91821pt}{6.29999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.98pt}{\resizebox{4.27098pt}{4.40999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.7pt}{\resizebox{3.57098pt}{3.15pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\parallel$}}}}}}\left(\nu,X_{N,\nu}\right)-\Lambda_{\mu}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.4pt}{\resizebox{5.91821pt}{6.29999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.4pt}{\resizebox{5.91821pt}{6.29999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.98pt}{\resizebox{4.27098pt}{4.40999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.7pt}{\resizebox{3.57098pt}{3.15pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\parallel$}}}}}}\left(\nu,X^{r}_{N,\nu}\right)\right],

\displaystyle\phi_{U}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)=\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\nu}\right)^{\top}g(\nu)\left[\mathcal{F}_{r}\left(X_{N}\right)(\nu)-\mathcal{F}_{r}\left(X^{r}_{N}\right)(\nu)\right],

\displaystyle\widetilde{\mathcal{U}}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)=\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\nu}\right)^{\top}g(\nu)\left(\mathcal{F}_{\mathcal{L}_{1}}-\mathcal{F}_{r}\right)(X_{N})(\nu).

Next, using the definition of
J_{\sigma}
in (
97
), we have that

\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\text{Tr}\left[K_{\sigma}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)\nabla^{2}\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\nu}\right)\right]=\text{Tr}\left[K_{\sigma}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)\right]=

\displaystyle\left\|J_{\sigma}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)\right\|_{F}^{2}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\left\|F_{\sigma}\left(\nu,X_{N,\nu}\right)-F_{\sigma}\left(\nu,X^{r}_{N,\nu}\right)\right\|_{F}^{2},

(D.29)

and

\displaystyle\nabla\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\nu}\right)^{\top}J_{\sigma}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)=\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\nu}\right)^{\top}\left(F_{\sigma}\left(\nu,X_{N,\nu}\right)-F_{\sigma}\left(\nu,X^{r}_{N,\nu}\right)\right).

(D.30)

As before, (
7
) in Assumption

allows us to write

\displaystyle F_{\sigma}\left(\nu,\cdot\right)=g(\nu)^{\perp}F^{\perp}_{\sigma}\left(\nu,\cdot\right)+g(\nu)F^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.4pt}{\resizebox{5.91821pt}{6.29999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.4pt}{\resizebox{5.91821pt}{6.29999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.98pt}{\resizebox{4.27098pt}{4.40999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.7pt}{\resizebox{3.57098pt}{3.15pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\parallel$}}}}}}_{\sigma}\left(\nu,\cdot\right),

which in turn lets us express (

\displaystyle\nabla\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\nu}\right)^{\top}J_{\sigma}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)=

\displaystyle\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\nu}\right)^{\top}g(\nu)\left(F^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.4pt}{\resizebox{5.91821pt}{6.29999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.4pt}{\resizebox{5.91821pt}{6.29999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.98pt}{\resizebox{4.27098pt}{4.40999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.7pt}{\resizebox{3.57098pt}{3.15pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\parallel$}}}}}}_{\sigma}\left(\nu,X_{N,\nu}\right)-F^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.4pt}{\resizebox{5.91821pt}{6.29999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.4pt}{\resizebox{5.91821pt}{6.29999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.98pt}{\resizebox{4.27098pt}{4.40999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.7pt}{\resizebox{3.57098pt}{3.15pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\parallel$}}}}}}_{\sigma}\left(\nu,X^{r}_{N,\nu}\right)\right)

\displaystyle+\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\nu}\right)^{\top}g(\nu)^{\perp}\left(F^{\perp}_{\sigma}\left(\nu,X_{N,\nu}\right)-F^{\perp}_{\sigma}\left(\nu,X^{r}_{N,\nu}\right)\right).

(D.31)

The expressions in (

), and (

) then lead to the desired result in (

∎

for all

for all

, where in the first integral, we switch between the variables

We then complete the proof by using an identical line of reasoning in the proof of Proposition

∎

Similar to Proposition
C.3
, we derive an alternative representation for the term
\mathcal{P}\left(\tau(t),\nu\right)
next.

Proposition D.6

Recall the expression for
\mathcal{P}\left(\tau(t),\nu\right)
in (
111
) in the statement of Lemma
4.5
which we restate below:

\displaystyle\mathcal{P}\left(\tau(t),\nu\right)=

\displaystyle\int_{\nu}^{\tau(t)}e^{(2\lambda-{\color[rgb]{1,0,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{1,0,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0}{1}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0}{1}{0}{0}\bm{\omega}})\beta}d_{\beta}\left[\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\beta}\right)^{\top}g(\beta)\right]\in\mathbb{R}^{1\times m},\quad 0\leq\nu\leq\tau(t),

(D.34)

where the
\tau(t)
is defined in (
104
).
Then,
\mathcal{P}\left(\tau(t),\nu\right)
admits the following representation:

\mathcal{P}\left(\tau(t),\nu\right)=\mathcal{P}_{\circ}\left(\tau(t),\nu\right)+\mathcal{P}_{ad}\left(\tau(t),\nu\right)+\widetilde{\mathcal{P}}\left(\tau(t),\nu\right)\in\mathbb{R}^{1\times m},\quad 0\leq\nu\leq\tau(t),~t\in\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0},

(D.35)

where

\displaystyle\mathcal{P}_{\circ}\left(\tau(t),\nu\right)=\int_{\nu}^{\tau(t)}e^{(2\lambda-{\color[rgb]{1,0,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{1,0,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0}{1}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0}{1}{0}{0}\bm{\omega}})\beta}\left(\mathcal{P}_{\mu}(\beta)d\beta+\mathcal{P}_{\sigma}(\beta)dW_{\beta}\right)^{\top},

(D.36a)

\displaystyle\mathcal{P}_{ad}\left(\tau(t),\nu\right)=\int_{\nu}^{\tau(t)}e^{(2\lambda-{\color[rgb]{1,0,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{1,0,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0}{1}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0}{1}{0}{0}\bm{\omega}})\beta}\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{U}}(\beta)^{\top}d\beta,\quad\widetilde{\mathcal{P}}\left(\tau(t),\nu\right)=\int_{\nu}^{\tau(t)}e^{(2\lambda-{\color[rgb]{1,0,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{1,0,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0}{1}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0}{1}{0}{0}\bm{\omega}})\beta}\widetilde{\mathcal{P}}_{\mathcal{U}}(\beta)^{\top}d\beta,

(D.36b)

and where
\mathcal{P}_{\mu}(\beta),~\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{U}}(\beta),~\widetilde{\mathcal{P}}_{\mathcal{U}}(\beta)\in\mathbb{R}^{m}
and
\mathcal{P}_{\sigma}(\beta)\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times d}
are defined using the expressions in (
103
) as

\displaystyle\mathcal{P}_{\mu}(\beta)=\dot{g}(\beta)^{\top}\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\beta}\right)+2g(\beta)^{\top}\left(\mathring{f}\left(\beta,Z_{N,\beta}\right)+\mathring{\Lambda}_{\mu}\left(\beta,Z_{N,\beta}\right)\right),

\displaystyle\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{U}}(\beta)=2g(\beta)^{\top}g(\beta)\mathring{\mathcal{F}}_{r}\left(Z_{N}\right)(\beta),\quad\widetilde{\mathcal{P}}_{\mathcal{U}}(\beta)=2g(\beta)^{\top}g(\beta)\left(\mathcal{F}_{\mathcal{L}_{1}}-\mathcal{F}_{r}\right)\left(X_{N}\right)(\beta),

\displaystyle\mathcal{P}_{\sigma}(\beta)=2g(\beta)^{\top}\mathring{F}_{\sigma}\left(\beta,Z_{N,\beta}\right).

Proof.

We closely follow the proof of Proposition
C.3
and begin by writing

\displaystyle\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\beta}\right)^{\top}g(\beta)=

\displaystyle\begin{bmatrix}\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\beta}\right)^{\top}g_{\cdot,1}(\beta)&\cdots&\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\beta}\right)^{\top}g_{\cdot,m}(\beta)\end{bmatrix}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle\begin{bmatrix}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\partial_{i}\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\beta}\right)g_{i,1}(\beta)&\cdots&\sum_{i=1}^{n}\partial_{i}\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\beta}\right)g_{i,m}(\beta)\end{bmatrix}\in\mathbb{R}^{1\times m},

(D.37)

where
g_{\cdot,j}(\beta)\in\mathbb{R}^{n}
is the
j
-th column of
g(\beta)
, and

\displaystyle\partial_{i}\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\beta}\right)\doteq\frac{\partial}{\partial\left(X_{N}-X^{r}_{N}\right)_{i}}\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\beta}\right)=2\left(X_{N,\beta}-X^{r}_{N,\beta}\right)_{i}\in\mathbb{R},\quad i\in\left\{1,\dots,n\right\}.

Applying Itô’s lemma to
\partial_{i}\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\beta}\right)g_{i,j}(\beta)\in\mathbb{R}
,
(i,j)\in\left\{1,\dots,n\right\}\times\left\{1,\dots,m\right\}
, and using the truncated dynamics in (
99

d_{\beta}\left[\partial_{i}\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\beta}\right)g_{i,j}(\beta)\right]=\left(\partial_{i}\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\beta}\right)\dot{g}_{i,j}(\beta)+\nabla\partial_{i}\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\beta}\right)^{\top}J_{\mu}\left(\beta,Z_{N,\beta}\right)g_{i,j}(\beta)\right)d\beta\\
+\nabla\partial_{i}\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\beta}\right)^{\top}J_{\sigma}\left(\beta,Z_{N,\beta}\right)g_{i,j}(\beta)dW_{\beta},

(D.38)

where we have used the straightforward fact that
\nabla^{2}\partial_{i}\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\beta}\right)=0\in\mathbb{S}^{n}
.
We have further replaced
J_{N,\mu}
and
J_{N,\sigma}
with
J_{\mu}
and
J_{\sigma}
because from Proposition
4.3
,
Z_{N,\beta}
is also a strong solution of the joint process (
97
) for all
\beta\in[\nu,\tau(t)]\subseteq[0,\tau^{\star}]\subseteq[0,\tau_{N}]
.
Observe from (
D
) that

\displaystyle d_{\beta}\left[\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\beta}\right)^{\top}g_{\cdot,j}(\beta)\right]=\sum_{i=1}^{n}d_{\beta}\left[\partial_{i}\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\beta}\right)g_{i,j}(\beta)\right]\in\mathbb{R},\quad j\in\left\{1,\dots,m\right\}.

It therefore follows from the expression in (
D.38
)

d_{\beta}\left[\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\beta}\right)^{\top}g_{\cdot,j}(\beta)\right]=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\left(\partial_{i}\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\beta}\right)\dot{g}_{i,j}(\beta)+\nabla\partial_{i}\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\beta}\right)^{\top}J_{\mu}\left(\beta,Z_{N,\beta}\right)g_{i,j}(\beta)\right)d\beta\\
+\sum_{i=1}^{n}\nabla\partial_{i}\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\beta}\right)^{\top}J_{\sigma}\left(\beta,Z_{N,\beta}\right)g_{i,j}(\beta)dW_{\beta},

which can be further written as

d_{\beta}\left[\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\beta}\right)^{\top}g_{\cdot,j}(\beta)\right]=\left(\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\beta}\right)^{\top}\dot{g}_{\cdot,j}(\beta)+g_{\cdot,j}(\beta)^{\top}\nabla\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\beta}\right)^{\top}J_{\mu}\left(\beta,Y_{N,\beta}\right)\right)d\beta\\
+g_{\cdot,j}(\beta)^{\top}\nabla\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\beta}\right)^{\top}J_{\sigma}\left(\beta,Z_{N,\beta}\right)dW_{\beta}\in\mathbb{R},

(D.39)

for
j\in\left\{1,\dots,m\right\}
.
Once again, (
D
) implies that

\displaystyle d_{\beta}\left[\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\beta}\right)^{\top}g(\beta)\right]=\begin{bmatrix}d_{\beta}\left[\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\beta}\right)^{\top}g_{\cdot,1}(\beta)\right]&\cdots&d_{\beta}\left[\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\beta}\right)^{\top}g_{\cdot,m}(\beta)\right]\end{bmatrix}\in\mathbb{R}^{1\times m}.

Thus, we use the expression in (
D.39
) to write

d_{\beta}\left[\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\beta}\right)^{\top}g(\beta)\right]=\left(\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\beta}\right)^{\top}\dot{g}(\beta)+\left(g(\beta)^{\top}\nabla\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\beta}\right)^{\top}J_{\mu}\left(\beta,Z_{N,\beta}\right)\right)^{\top}\right)d\beta\\
+\left(g(\beta)^{\top}\nabla\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\beta}\right)^{\top}J_{\sigma}\left(\beta,Z_{N,\beta}\right)dW_{\beta}\right)^{\top}\in\mathbb{R}^{1\times m}.

(D.40)

Now, since
Z_{N}=X_{N}-X^{r}_{N}
, using the definition of the gradient of vector valued functions in Sec.
1.4
, we observe that

\displaystyle\nabla\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\beta}\right)=2\begin{bmatrix}\nabla\left(X_{N,\beta}-X^{r}_{N,\beta}\right)_{1}&\cdots&\nabla\left(X_{N,\beta}-X^{r}_{N,\beta}\right)_{n}\end{bmatrix}=

\displaystyle 2\begin{bmatrix}\nabla\left(Z_{N,\beta}\right)_{1}&\cdots&\nabla\left(Z_{N,\beta}\right)_{n}\end{bmatrix}

\displaystyle=

\displaystyle 2\mathbb{I}_{n}\in\mathbb{S}^{n}.

Thus, it follows from the definitions of the vector fields in (
97
) that

\displaystyle\nabla\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\beta}\right)^{\top}J_{\mu}\left(\beta,Z_{N,\beta}\right)=

\displaystyle 2\left(F_{\mu}\left(\beta,X_{N,\beta},U_{\mathcal{L}_{1},\beta}\right)-F_{\mu}\left(\beta,X^{r}_{N,\beta},U^{r}_{\beta}\right)\right)

\displaystyle\overset{(\star)}{=}

\displaystyle 2\mathring{f}\left(\beta,Z_{N,\beta}\right)+2g(\beta)\left(\mathcal{F}_{\mathcal{L}_{1}}-\mathcal{F}_{r}\right)\left(X_{N}\right)(\beta)+2g(\beta)\mathring{\mathcal{F}}_{r}\left(Z_{N}\right)(\beta)

\displaystyle\hskip 199.16928pt+2\mathring{\Lambda}_{\mu}\left(\beta,Z_{N,\beta}\right)\in\mathbb{R}^{n},

\displaystyle\nabla\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\beta}\right)^{\top}J_{\sigma}\left(\beta,Z_{N,\beta}\right)=

\displaystyle 2\left(F_{\sigma}\left(\beta,X_{N,\beta}\right)-F_{\sigma}\left(\beta,X^{r}_{N,\beta}\right)\right)=2\mathring{F}_{\sigma}\left(\beta,Z_{N,\beta}\right)\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d},

where we obtain
(\star)
by using the decomposition from (
3
) in Definition
1
to obtain

\displaystyle F_{\mu}\left(\beta,X_{N,\beta},U_{\mathcal{L}_{1},\beta}\right)-F_{\mu}\left(\beta,X^{r}_{N,\beta},U^{r}_{\beta}\right)

\displaystyle=\bar{F}_{\mu}\left(\beta,X_{N,\beta}\right)-\bar{F}_{\mu}\left(\beta,X^{r}_{N,\beta}\right)+g(\beta)\left(U_{\mathcal{L}_{1},\beta}-U^{r}_{\beta}\right)+\Lambda_{\mu}\left(\beta,X_{N,\beta}\right)-\Lambda_{\mu}\left(\beta,X^{r}_{N,\beta}\right)

\displaystyle=\mathring{f}\left(\beta,Z_{N,\beta}\right)+g(\beta)\left(\mathcal{F}_{\mathcal{L}_{1}}-\mathcal{F}_{r}\right)\left(X_{N}\right)(\beta)+g(\beta)\mathring{\mathcal{F}}_{r}\left(Z_{N}\right)(\beta)+\mathring{\Lambda}_{\mu}\left(\beta,Z_{N,\beta}\right),

and where we have also used (
D
) in the proof of Proposition
D.4
.
Substituting the above identities into (
D.40
) produces

\displaystyle d_{\beta}\left[\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\beta}\right)^{\top}g(\beta)\right]=\left[\mathcal{P}_{\mu}(\beta)+\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{U}}(\beta)+\widetilde{\mathcal{P}}_{\mathcal{U}}(\beta)\right]^{\top}d\beta+\left[\mathcal{P}_{\sigma}(\beta)dW_{\beta}\right]^{\top}\in\mathbb{R}^{1\times m}.

Then, (
D.35
) is established by substituting the above into (
D.34
).

∎

The next result establishes the bounds for the pertinent entities derived in the last proposition.

Proposition D.7

Consider the functions
\mathcal{P}_{\mu}(t)\in\mathbb{R}^{m}
and
\mathcal{P}_{\sigma}(t)\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times d}
defined in the statement of Proposition
D.6
.
If the stopping time
\tau^{\star}
, defined in (
104
), Lemma
4.5
, satisfies
\tau^{\star}=t^{\star}
, then

\displaystyle\sup_{\nu\in[0,t^{\star}]}\left\|\mathcal{P}_{\mu}(\nu)\right\|_{L_{2{\mathsf{p}}}}\leq 2\Delta_{g}\Delta_{\mathcal{P}_{\mu}}({\mathsf{p}})+\Delta_{\dot{g}}\sup_{\nu\in[0,t^{\star}]}\left\|\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\nu}\right)\right\|_{L_{2{\mathsf{p}}}},

(D.41a)

\displaystyle\sup_{\nu\in[0,t^{\star}]}\left\|\mathcal{P}_{\sigma}(\nu)\right\|_{L_{\mathsf{q}}}\leq 2\Delta_{g}\Delta_{\mathcal{P}_{\sigma}}({\mathsf{p}}),

(D.41b)

where

\displaystyle\Delta_{\mathcal{P}_{\mu}}({\mathsf{p}})=\sup_{\nu\in[0,t^{\star}]}\left(\left\|\mathring{f}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)\right\|_{L_{2{\mathsf{p}}}}+\left\|\mathring{\Lambda}_{\mu}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)\right\|_{L_{2{\mathsf{p}}}}\right),\quad\Delta_{\mathcal{P}_{\sigma}}({\mathsf{p}})=\sup_{\nu\in[0,t^{\star}]}\left\|\mathring{F}_{\sigma}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)\right\|_{L_{2{\mathsf{p}}}}.

Proof.

We have the following bound for the term
\mathcal{P}_{\mu}
defined in (
D.36a
):

\displaystyle\left\|\mathcal{P}_{\mu}(\nu)\right\|\leq

\displaystyle\left\|\dot{g}(\nu)\right\|_{F}\left\|\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\nu}\right)\right\|+2\left\|g(\nu)\right\|_{F}\left(\left\|\mathring{f}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)\right\|+\left\|\mathring{\Lambda}_{\mu}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)\right\|\right)

\displaystyle\leq

\displaystyle\Delta_{\dot{g}}\left\|\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\nu}\right)\right\|+2\Delta_{g}\left(\left\|\mathring{f}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)\right\|+\left\|\mathring{\Lambda}_{\mu}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)\right\|\right),\quad\forall\nu\in[0,t^{\star}],

where we have used the bounds on
g(t)
and
\dot{g}(t)
in Assumption
1
.
It then follows from the Minkowski’s inequality that

\displaystyle\left\|\mathcal{P}_{\mu}(\nu)\right\|_{L_{2{\mathsf{p}}}}\leq

\displaystyle\Delta_{\dot{g}}\left\|\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\nu}\right)\right\|_{L_{2{\mathsf{p}}}}+2\Delta_{g}\left(\left\|\mathring{f}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)\right\|_{L_{2{\mathsf{p}}}}+\left\|\mathring{\Lambda}_{\mu}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)\right\|_{L_{2{\mathsf{p}}}}\right),\quad\forall\nu\in[0,t^{\star}],

which in turn implies (
D.41a
).
The bound in (
D.41b
) follows trivially.
∎

The next lemma establishes the bound on
\Xi
.

Lemma D.1

Consider the term
\Xi\left(\tau(t),Z_{N}\right)
defined in (
107a
), Lemma
4.5
.
If the stopping time
\tau^{\star}
, defined in (
104
), Lemma
4.5
, satisfies
\tau^{\star}=t^{\star}
, then:

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[e^{-2\lambda t}\Xi\left(t,Z_{N}\right)\right]\leq\frac{\Delta_{\Xi_{1}}(1,t^{\star})}{2\lambda},

(D.42a)

\displaystyle\left\|e^{-2\lambda t}\Xi\left(t,Z_{N}\right)\right\|_{L_{{\mathsf{p}}}}\leq\frac{\Delta_{\Xi_{1}}({\mathsf{p}},t^{\star})}{2\lambda}+\frac{\Delta_{\Xi_{2}}({\mathsf{p}},t^{\star})}{2\sqrt{\lambda}},

(D.42b)

for all
(t,{\mathsf{p}})\in[0,t^{\star}]\times\mathbb{N}_{\geq 2}
, where

\displaystyle\Delta_{\Xi_{1}}({\mathsf{p}},t^{\star})=\sup_{\nu\in[0,t^{\star}]}\left(\Delta_{g}^{\perp}\left\|\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\nu}\right)\right\|_{L_{2{\mathsf{p}}}}\left\|\mathring{\Lambda}^{\perp}_{\mu}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)\right\|_{L_{2{\mathsf{p}}}}+\left(\left\|\mathring{F}_{\sigma}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)\right\|_{L_{2{\mathsf{p}}}}\right)^{2}\right),

\displaystyle\Delta_{\Xi_{2}}({\mathsf{p}},t^{\star})=\Delta_{g}^{\perp}\mathfrak{p}({\mathsf{p}})\sup_{\nu\in[0,t^{\star}]}\left\|\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\nu}\right)\right\|_{L_{2{\mathsf{p}}}}\left\|\mathring{F}^{\perp}_{\sigma}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)\right\|_{L_{2{\mathsf{p}}}}.

Proof.

Note that
\tau(t)\in[0,t^{\star}]
since
\tau^{\star}=t^{\star}
.
Thus, in the following, we replace
\tau(t)
with
t
with the condition that
t\in[0,t^{\star}]
.
We then begin by writing

\displaystyle e^{-2\lambda t}\Xi\left(t,Z_{N}\right)=e^{-2\lambda t}\int_{0}^{t}e^{2\lambda\nu}\phi_{\mu}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)d\nu+e^{-2\lambda t}\int_{0}^{t}e^{2\lambda\nu}\phi_{\sigma}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)dW_{\nu},\quad t\in[0,t^{\star}].

(D.43)

The regularity assumptions and the
t
-continuity of the strong solutions
X_{N,t}
and
X^{r}_{N,t}
imply that
\phi_{\sigma}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)\in\mathcal{M}^{loc}_{2}\left(\mathbb{R}^{1\times d}|\mathfrak{W}_{t}\right)
.
Hence, taking the expectation of both sides of (
D.43
) and using
[
91
, Thm. 1.5.21]
produces

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[e^{-2\lambda t}\Xi\left(t,Z_{N}\right)\right]=

\displaystyle e^{-2\lambda t}\mathbb{E}\left[\int_{0}^{t}e^{2\lambda\nu}\phi_{\mu}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)d\nu\right]

\displaystyle\leq

\displaystyle e^{-2\lambda t}\mathbb{E}\left[\int_{0}^{t}e^{2\lambda\nu}\left|\phi_{\mu}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)\right|d\nu\right],\quad\forall t\in[0,t^{\star}],

(D.44)

where we have used the fact that since
\tau^{\star}=t^{\star}
, and
t^{\star}
is a constant,

\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[e^{-2\lambda t}\right]=e^{-2\lambda t},\quad\forall t\in[0,t^{\star}].

Using the fact above, we further apply the Minkowski’s inequality to (
D.43
) and obtain

\left\|e^{-2\lambda t}\Xi\left(t,Z_{N}\right)\right\|_{L_{{\mathsf{p}}}}\leq e^{-2\lambda t}\left\|\int_{0}^{t}e^{2\lambda\nu}\phi_{\mu}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)d\nu\right\|_{L_{{\mathsf{p}}}}\\
+e^{-2\lambda t}\left\|\int_{0}^{t}e^{2\lambda\nu}\phi_{\sigma}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)dW_{\nu}\right\|_{L_{{\mathsf{p}}}},\quad\forall(t,{\mathsf{p}})\in[0,t^{\star}]\times\mathbb{N}_{\geq 2}.

(D.45)

The regularity assumptions on the vector fields and the
t
-continuity of the strong solutions
X_{N,t}
and
X^{r}_{N,t}
over
[0,t^{\star}]\subseteq[0,\tau_{N}]
imply that
\phi_{\mu}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)\in\mathcal{M}^{loc}_{2}\left(\mathbb{R}|\mathfrak{W}_{t}\right)
.
Thus, we invoke Proposition
B.1
for
\left\{\theta,\xi,n_{s},S\right\}=\left\{2\lambda,0,1,\phi_{\mu}\left(\cdot,Z_{N}\right)\right\}
to obtain

\displaystyle\left\|\int_{0}^{t}e^{2\lambda\nu}\left|\phi_{\mu}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)\right|d\nu\right\|_{L_{{\mathsf{p}}}}\leq

\displaystyle\frac{e^{2\lambda t}}{2\lambda}\sup_{\nu\in[0,t^{\star}]}\left\|\phi_{\mu}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)\right\|_{L_{\mathsf{p}}},\quad\forall(t,{\mathsf{p}})\in[0,t^{\star}]\times\mathbb{N}_{\geq 1},

where we have bounded
e^{2\lambda t}-1
by
e^{2\lambda t}
.
Using the definition of
\phi_{\mu}
in (
108
), we can further bound the above by invoking the Minkowski’s and Cauchy-Schwarz inequalities:

\left\|\int_{0}^{t}e^{2\lambda\nu}\left|\phi_{\mu}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)\right|d\nu\right\|_{L_{{\mathsf{p}}}}\\
\leq\frac{e^{2\lambda t}}{2\lambda}\sup_{\nu\in[0,t^{\star}]}\left(\Delta_{g}^{\perp}\left\|\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\nu}\right)\right\|_{L_{2{\mathsf{p}}}}\left\|\mathring{\Lambda}^{\perp}_{\mu}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)\right\|_{L_{2{\mathsf{p}}}}+\left(\left\|\mathring{F}_{\sigma}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)\right\|_{L_{2{\mathsf{p}}}}\right)^{2}\right),

(D.46)

for all
(t,{\mathsf{p}})\in[0,t^{\star}]\times\mathbb{N}_{\geq 1}
, where we have also used the bound on
g(\nu)^{\perp}
in Assumption
1
.

Next, we have the following from the definition of
\phi_{\sigma}
in (
108
):

\displaystyle\int_{0}^{t}e^{2\lambda\nu}\phi_{\sigma}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)dW_{\nu}=\int_{0}^{t}e^{2\lambda\nu}\left(\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\nu}\right)^{\top}g(\nu)^{\perp}\mathring{F}^{\perp}_{\sigma}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)\right)dW_{\nu}.

We bound the above by using Lemma
B.2
with
\left\{\theta,\xi,n_{l},n_{q},Q\right\}=\left\{2\lambda,0,1,d,W\right\}
, and

\displaystyle L(\nu)=\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\nu}\right)^{\top}g(\nu)^{\perp}\mathring{F}^{\perp}_{\sigma}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right),

to obtain

\left\|\int_{0}^{t}e^{2\lambda\nu}\phi_{\sigma}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)dW_{\nu}\right\|_{L_{\mathsf{p}}}\\
\begin{aligned} &\leq\mathfrak{p}({\mathsf{p}})\frac{e^{2\lambda t}}{2\sqrt{\lambda}}\sup_{\nu\in[0,t^{\star}]}\left\|\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\nu}\right)^{\top}g(\nu)^{\perp}\mathring{F}^{\perp}_{\sigma}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)\right\|_{L_{{\mathsf{p}}}}\\
&\leq\mathfrak{p}({\mathsf{p}})\Delta_{g}^{\perp}\frac{e^{2\lambda t}}{2\sqrt{\lambda}}\sup_{\nu\in[0,t^{\star}]}\left\|\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\nu}\right)\right\|_{L_{2{\mathsf{p}}}}\left\|\mathring{F}^{\perp}_{\sigma}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)\right\|_{L_{2{\mathsf{p}}}},\quad\forall(t,{\mathsf{p}})\in[0,t^{\star}]\times\mathbb{N}_{\geq 2},\end{aligned}

(D.47)

where we have bounded
\left(e^{4\lambda t}-1\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}
by
e^{2\lambda t}
and used the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality to obtain the last inequality.

Substituting (
D.46
) into (
D
) leads to

\mathbb{E}\left[e^{-2\lambda t}\Xi\left(t,Z_{N}\right)\right]\\
\leq\frac{1}{2\lambda}\sup_{\nu\in[0,t^{\star}]}\left(\Delta_{g}^{\perp}\left\|\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\nu}\right)\right\|_{L_{2}}\left\|\mathring{\Lambda}^{\perp}_{\mu}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)\right\|_{L_{2}}+\left(\left\|\mathring{F}_{\sigma}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)\right\|_{L_{2}}\right)^{2}\right),\quad\forall t\in[0,t^{\star}].

(D.48)

Similarly, substituting (
D.46
) and (
D.47
) into (
D.45
) produces

\begin{aligned} &\left\|e^{-2\lambda t}\Xi\left(t,Z_{N}\right)\right\|_{L_{{\mathsf{p}}}}\\
&\leq\Delta_{g}^{\perp}\frac{\mathfrak{p}({\mathsf{p}})}{2\sqrt{\lambda}}\sup_{\nu\in[0,t^{\star}]}\left\|\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\nu}\right)\right\|_{L_{2{\mathsf{p}}}}\left\|\mathring{F}^{\perp}_{\sigma}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)\right\|_{L_{2{\mathsf{p}}}}\end{aligned}\\
+\frac{1}{2\lambda}\sup_{\nu\in[0,t^{\star}]}\left(\Delta_{g}^{\perp}\left\|\partial\mathcal{V}\left(Z_{N,\nu}\right)\right\|_{L_{2{\mathsf{p}}}}\left\|\mathring{\Lambda}^{\perp}_{\mu}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)\right\|_{L_{2{\mathsf{p}}}}+\left(\left\|\mathring{F}_{\sigma}\left(\nu,Z_{N,\nu}\right)\right\|_{L_{2{\mathsf{p}}}}\right)^{2}\right),

(D.49)

for all
(t,{\mathsf{p}})\in[0,t^{\star}]\times\mathbb{N}_{\geq 2}
.
We have thus established the bounds in (
D.42
).

∎

for

, and where

for all

Proposition D.12

\times\left(\int_{0}^{\nu}e^{{\color[rgb]{1,0,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{1,0,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0}{1}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0}{1}{0}{0}\bm{\omega}}\beta}\left[\mathring{\Lambda}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.4pt}{\resizebox{5.91821pt}{6.29999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.4pt}{\resizebox{5.91821pt}{6.29999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.98pt}{\resizebox{4.27098pt}{4.40999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.7pt}{\resizebox{3.57098pt}{3.15pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\parallel$}}}}}}_{\mu}\left(\beta,Z_{N,\beta}\right)d\beta+\mathring{F}^{\mathchoice{\raisebox{-1.4pt}{\resizebox{5.91821pt}{6.29999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\displaystyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-1.4pt}{\resizebox{5.91821pt}{6.29999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.75pt}{$\textstyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.98pt}{\resizebox{4.27098pt}{4.40999pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{1.22499pt}{$\scriptstyle\parallel$}}}}}{\raisebox{-0.7pt}{\resizebox{3.57098pt}{3.15pt}{\hbox{\raisebox{0.875pt}{$\scriptscriptstyle\parallel$}}}}}}_{\sigma}\left(\beta,Z_{N,\beta}\right)dW_{\beta}\right]\right)d\nu,\quad(j,t)\in\left\{1,\dots,4\right\}\times[{\color[rgb]{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0.0600000000000001,0.46,1}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@stroke{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\pgfsys@color@cmyk@fill{0.94}{0.54}{0}{0}\bm{T_{s}}},t^{\star}],

,
